title: So disappointed! No longer recommend. Seller never responded.
body: FRUIT FLY SEASON IS RAPIDLY APPROACHING AND I'M DETERMINED TO PREVENT LAST SUMMER'S INFESTATION. Update : I contacted the company multiple ways and multiple times. Amazon and the company totally ignored my legitimate complaint. Obviously they don't care about their customers dissatisfaction. It's not about the money - it's about blatant misrepresentation and unethical behavior displayed by both companies. I couldn't even get Amazon to include the "frequently returned" box on the item's page. I bought three bottles of auntie's product on Amazon 6 days ago to replace my DIY liquid attractant of appl cider vinegar +brown sugar +dish detergent. It's been 5 days and can confirm the other negative reviews that the product CAN'T contain the same liquid attractant - the fruit flies feed on the liquid and are not trapped - they can fly away!!! I unintentionally performed a side by side experiment using this WORTHLESS product against my attractant. Both liquids were placed next to separate hanging cylinders of bright yellow sticky fly paper. I actually watched the flies fly from the auntie's product into my liquid. Unlike the auntie product, any flies that were not trapped in my DIY liquid were trapped in the fly paper. After 5 days I had to replace the fly paper adjacent to DIY liquid. in contrast, the 3 bottles of Auntie containing who knows what had A TOTAL OF LESS THAN 20 IN THE BOTTLES AND ABOUT 10 TO 20 TRAPPED BY THE FLY PAPER. I am so angry about wasting money on products from Amazon with good reviews. This product has overall rating of 3.8. But that rating is CUMULATIVE - The much older reviews are generally positive compared to more current negative reviews. I conclude this is due to a change in formulation that neither amazon or the seller made clear. I was so pleased that Good Housekeeping had recommended the best way to eliminates fruit fly infestations in a recent article. The GH panel incorrectly included this product as the only commercially effective liquid attractant since it contained malic acid as part of the formulation. The FRUIT FLY SEASON article made me remember that I had used Aunties successfully a few summers ago and loved their esthetics and effectiveness. I already emailed a request for them to provide evidence of its effectiveness using a recent bottle. I am requesting a refund from this seller based on my results and will update the status with both responses. Meanwhile if you are battling with fruit flies, infestations made worse by the higher temperature (I live in Connecticut) in the Northeast, read below. First understand that you must use the following steps throughout the fruit fly lifecycle (over several weeks so that the original fruit flies are trapped as well as the their progeny hatched from the hundreds of larvae deposited on whatever they fed on. {I am a biochemist and patent attorney so I needed to know what was going on}. Keep in mind for DIY solutions or other traps that you must attract and rid them from escaping. Otherwise you'll have dead flies near and flying around the attractant. A single fruit fly will deposit hundreds of larvae on fruit and vegetables and existing food sources. Follow these steps : 1. Clean all surfaces daily with your typical all purpose cleaner (I use Fantastic with bleach) wherever you find these annoying bugs. For us this is primarily the kitchen in addition to the bathroom and TV room. REMEMBER THEY ARE ATTRACTED TO LIGHT AND 1 FLY WILL DEPOSIT EGGS THAT MATURE IN about 5 to7 DAYS. 2. Unfortunately surface cleaning every 1-2 days is necessary to eliminate flying flies you see and larva that will hatch that you can't. 3. Immediately thoroughly wash all fruit and vegetables (existing or new) and refrigerate. 4. Eliminate All food debris from kitchen counters, microwave, garbage cans, toaster oven, pet water and food bowls, etc. and keep everything covered or washed like used knives, glassware and plates. 5. If you think this is drastic like I did, then you will see an infestation that feels as if those little things won... 6. in the article, Good housekeeping recommended this product as using malic acid which is found in apple cider vinegar. It was part of discussion on using a DIY solution see ingredients above. Any solution must also contain a detergent which causes the flies eating on the attractant liguid to sink in the solution. They can't fly away and begin a new cycle of depositing eggs. At the beginning of the infestation I used the ingredients above along with standing/hanging yellow sticky fly paper I also bought from Amazon. I am very frustrated that I didn't do the research and work upfront instead of wasting money trying to find the non-existent magic bullet all summer!! As much as I love tasty vine ripened tomatoes and other summer fruit and vegetables, it's just not worth it. I think the high temperatures in July throughout the North East as well as nationaly/globally contributed to the problem experienced by me and almost everyone I know.

title: Six Traps Set - One Fly Caught. 80 Bucks Wasted
body: What I liked: It's easy to use. What I disliked: It arrived 2 days late. It doesn't work. It's a spill hazard. It's extremely expensive considering it's vinegar, water, fruit juice and soap. I paid $80 to catch one fly. That about sums it up. We get these fruit flies every year but this year is the worst. I've had the drains cleaned and treated professionally and I'm pouring drain cleaner and fly treatment down the drains daily. I was going to buy the decoy traps that look like an apple. I've used them before and they were great. I couldn't find any in stock, except for one that had bad reviews. Then there was Aunt Fannie's. There's no special formula even though Aunt Fannie's has a patent on their formula. It's different because first, it's not a decorative decoy trap that looks like an apple or mini pumpkin. Aunt Fannie's looks like a spice bottle. When I opened the cap, I expected to see some kind of funnel mechanism on top. That's how the other traps work. The flies are attracted by the sweet formula inside. They slide down the funnel right into the solution and can't get out. Aunt Fannie's just has a wide-mouth opening that can very easily spill. I placed 4 in my kitchen, one in the dining room and one in a bathroom - where the flies congregate as the directions tell you. I watched the flies swarm around the traps and sat back waiting for them to dive in and never check out. They landed on the bottles, walked around, climbed down inside, climbed back out, walked around a little more, then swarmed around. One little fly fell in and couldn't swim. So $80, several days of waiting, then placing these open bottles of liquid all over the place, and I caught one, single fly. Just one. I was convinced to buy this product because I saw so many great reviews. It seemed like a no-brainer when I couldn't find the product I actually wanted. I've never had this happen before. I usually buy stuff with 4 stars or better and when I do, I agree with those reviews. In this case, I was completely wrong and I've wasted time and money.

I was thinking maybe its because the opening is the size of the packaging. Most fly traps have tiny openings so they cant get back out. I purchased the apples ones as well. Once those were opened they went right to them. Lots of dead flies in those! So I believe this is a hit or miss for anyone who purchases.

I will not purchase again. Does not work.

body: Aunt Fannie’s Flying Punch is a joke. Three bottles out for one month while fruit flies are doing summersaults around my face taunting me as they exclaim “I’m s that all you got?” Seriously don’t buy this. It doesn’t work. Just donate the money to someone who needs it on the street.

title: Didn’t work for me
body: I haven’t caught not one gnat or fly I placed it on my kitchen sink counter around my plants! I have a zevo and sticky traps that work. Every thing catching them except for the punch I even sat it in the pot of one of my plants and still didn’t catch not one gnats

title: Works terribly; less effective than DIY traps and smells terrible.
body: My high rise condo is currently having trash chute issues, so I came home from a weekend trip to a fruit fly problem. I hastily bought this, a blue light/sticky trap, and placed out a few cups with old wine and a drop of dish soap. Left all of these out for 2 full days throughout the kitchen to eliminate my new roommates. The fruit flies are all now gone, but no thanks to this product (or the light trap, while I'm at it). The 2 cups of old wine, however, successfully caught and drowned dozens of fruit flies each. The light trap managed to catch one. This product caught zero. It also reeks of vinegar, strongly enough that I notice it immediately upon entering the apartment. I highly recommending skipping this entirely and putting out old wine or juice with dish soap instead, save your money and your sense of smell.

title: Boooooo Boooooo 👎🏾
body: If I could rate this zero stars or negatives stars I would!!!! This sucks I have a fruit fly infestation I have let this out and the flies are going nowhere near it. It’s literally nothing but apple cider vinegar I coilda bought a bottle cheaper . I WANT MY MONEY BACK

title: Possibly Slipped Past Quality Control???
body: I have never been as disappointed in something from Amazon as I was with this stuff! I had seen them mention it on a TV show. Im thinking maybe GMA...but anyway....so then i checked AZ and it had a ton of positive reviews so I just knew this was going to be the answer to our fruit fly problem. In another few days it will be an entire month that these 2 bottles have sat out in our house where we see these flies the most. Believe it or not....not one single fruit fly is in the liquid of either of these! We've stood and watched them fly to the bottle, and even down in it but pretty soon they fly right back out! Finally yesterday I decided to top each one of them off with a bit more apple cider vinegar..thinking POSSIBLY it hadnt been strong enough originally. NOPE! It's still not working. But yet there are still people saying it worked great for them. So Ive finally started a return today since I feel like Ive given it a decent chance with no success.

title: Product does not deliver advertised results...
body: I am not sure where they came from (or keep coming from), but I have a small swarm of fruit flies in my kitchen that I have been trying to get rid of for several weeks. I take my trash out daily, have cleaned my kitchen from top to bottom including the drains and trash can, no longer leave fruit (or any other kind of food) out on the counter, and have moved my cat's food and water dishes to another room. I also have tried several DIY natural remedies. Yet the fruit flies persist. I do not want to use an insecticide spray in my home because I have multiple chemical sensitivities. I read about Aunt Fannie's online -- the product got good reviews, so I thought it would be worth a try. The Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch! arrived and I put it out on the counter above where my kitchen trash can is and waited hopefully for it to work its magic. It has been five days and I am still waiting. In five days, Aunt Fannie's has trapped five fruit flies. In the same time period, I have swatted down 29 fruit flies and a sinkful of soapy water that I soaked a couple of pots in for an hour one day trapped seven fruit flies. I am really disappointed in this product -- it was definitely not worth the money. At this point, I am not sure what will work to rid my kitchen or fruit flies, but I feel fairly certain that it will not be Aunt Fannie's.

title: Don't buy this. Make your own!
body: Well, I got duped by this product. It's mostly my fault. I needed a way to get rid of fruit flies that made their way into my home. I had made my own trap with apple cider vinegar and dish soap, but the vinegar was really bad and stunk up the house. I searched for fruit fly traps and came across this. I gleaned over the description and didn't bother with the reviews (two things I usually never do) and ordered it. It arrived the next day (which is why I bought it) and I opened the package. Much to my surprise and disappointment, it was just a small bottle of apple cider vinegar with soap in it. Man, I felt dumb, but I decided to try it. The cap is a joke. It makes the bottle taller when open and easier to knock over so you can spill it everywhere. Also, it leaks if you close it and don't keep it upright. I poured some into a glass pudding bowl, covered it with plastic wrap and sealed it with a rubber band around the bowl. I poked four 3/8" holes in the wrap, set it out near where the flies are and left for a few minutes. When I came back the flies were all over the bowl. Once they make their way in through the holes they're essentially trapped. You will get the same results with apple cider vinegar and dish soap with this setup (because that's all it is) and over time it'll be cheaper. Don't buy this or any other similar brands. Just make your own trap and save the $8 that I stupidly spent.

title: More still flying around than dying
body: I've used Aunt Fanny's ant spray in the past with good results. So I thought, why not try the fruit fly solution for those pesky pests? Well, here's a good reason: it doesn't work very well. Sure, I see some floating in the liquid, but there are at least ten times that are still flying all around my kitchen. Then I decided to try one that sticks to the wall with good reviews. But those fell off the wall and I will return them. So I will buy the ones I should have all along, Terro traps. They worked great and I'm embarrassed that I bothered with anything else. I just wish Terro sold the liquid which how this all began.

title: You can do better
body: I had a THICK CLOUD of fruit flies descend in my kitchen! Researching my options, I found this product & ordered a bottle. While I was desperately awaiting its arrival, however, I fell back on 2 older remedies—beer and apple cider vinegar. Maybe 1/8 of a cup of each of these were poured into separate clean cat food tins with some dish soap for viscosity, then covered with plastic wrap, and punctured with small holes. Once the product arrived, I could easily compare the attraction each liquid possessed. Beer? The winner! Apple cider vinegar? A very close second! Lagging way WAY behind is this product. Granted, it’s got a small number of snagged victims, but nothing like the other two. Save yourself some money. You also get the freebie bonus of finishing off the beer that didn’t get poured into the can!

title: Waste of money

body: This item did not work for me. We followed the instructions and while it did catch some fruit flies, they mostly just hung around the open lid and didn’t actually go into the container. I feel like the design is a bit flawed with that because if the flys go in there is nothing trapping them and they can just fly out. It is easy to use but not very effective. I think if you poured the liquid into something that would actually catch the flys themselves it would work great but again I think the design is a bit flawed.

body: Items arrived leaking, with one container's top fully off and the other half off and the plastic wrapping the two torn. The fruit flies were having a field day on my counter!

title: Don’t waste your money
body: Don’t waste your money. Good old apple cider vinegar works better. Pour 1/4c of acv into a small bowl, cover with plastic wrap and poke small holes in the plastic. It actually works better and doesn’t emit any smell like this product.

title: Aunt Fannie's - Needs improvement
body: Gnats (fruit flies) just hang around the liquid but don't attempt to get in. I suggest the company to make these containers very small with a sticky plastic inside so they can get trapped. The idea is great but the designed is terrible. I don't know what to do with it but I am probably just going to have to throw it away unless the company offers a refund.

body: Two of the four bottles had loose lids and leaked. Waste of my time and money. Need to return.

title: Didn't work for me

title: Save your money - cheap wine and suds are far better
body: I wanted to like the ease of use and disposability of this product, but it simply did not work and in my experience, was poorly designed. Like most fruit fly-killing concoctions, it had vinegar and dish soap. But judging by the scent, that was about it. No sweetness I could detect (admittedly I don’t know what they are attracted to precisely).Judging by the way they swarmed fruit juice or wine, that seems like a requirement. Also, while the slim container is convenient, a short open glass provided significantly more surface area, which presumably made it easier for them to land. Bottom line, the side by side trial I ran with a glass of red wine, white wine and this product. No comparison. Wines in a landslide of fly carcasses.

title: Paying for packaging
body: This product does work, sort of, for attracting fruit flies. However for the price, you can do just as well to buy the little red plastic apple baits at the grocery. Even better, just use cider vinegar in a trap, because that's basically what this is. I use it as an attractant for a heavy duty fly stick, but red wine or cider vinegar work just as well. I didn't actually catch a whole lot of flies in the little jars.

title: Don't buy
body: Not as powerful as making home remedy

title: Kills, yes...but also attracts.
body: This has been a particularly bad year for fruit flies and gnats down South, and so I needed a little extra help. I love Aunt Fannie's household products, but this one is not one that I will purchase again. The solution inside these containers do kill the pests, but it also attracts them. For every 10 little darlings floating in the bottle, there are 20 more buzzing and crawling around the container, which defeats the purpose. Also, the open container design emits a very strong vinegar odor throughout the house...which I suppose is better than a chemical smell, but it still is unpleasant. The open container design also invites spillage is accidentally knocked over, which is easy to do when participating in food prep.

title: So far, the flies are not going for it.
body: The products was supposed to attract the flies and kill them, right? Well the flies are still buzzing around happily. If however, the product was meant to be Birth control for flies, its efficacy remains to be seen I suppose.

title: What a mess
body: I can’t speak to how well this works but I can tell you almost everyone of the 6 I bought leaked. I could smell vinegar before I opened the box, when I got into it the box was wet as were each of the jars. Every lid was loose and even with an inner seal they had all leaked. What a mess, had to clean them up before even trying to use them. I can’t imagine ordering any more.

title: I'm beginning to think it's attracting more bugs, rather than eliminating them.
body: I bought two, and when I open the lid, I get lots of little fruit flies around the jars -- and most especially on the lid rather than inside the jars. It seems to attract more fruit flies than I saw initially. I tend to wonder if flies from elsewhere (outside?) are finding their way inside to get to these little jars. I have cleaned and cleaned, and I can't seem to find a source of these little bugs. I have no fruit sitting out, or any other exposed food. I'm wondering if they're coming from the kitchen drain, so I bought some stuff to pour down the drain that's supposed to work for killing a variety of flies, but it hasn't arrived yet. So the fight continues... sooner or later, I'll rid myself of these little buggers.

title: We had high hopes this would be the answer
body: Our office goes through periods where we seem to be deviled by very small flying insects, they could be gnats or fruit flies, we don't know for sure but this product has the ingredients that are recommended to work on either. We have never found a dead insect in the bottles and we still had the problem on going. We didn't have that many but they were persistent and annoying. We are in a lull currently and I'd love to say it was this product but neither of the two bottles I bought have shown any dead in them so so far, we'd have to say they didn't work for us.

title: I'm Not Sure Why There's a Lid
body: The lid seems to just be there for cosmetic effect. It closes, it seems secure, but you can still smell the vinegar coming through. Turn the bottle upside down, and it leaks out pretty heavily. I discovered this flaw after my cat knocked the bottle over and, closed lid and all, about 1/4th of the fluid leaked out everywhere. I'm sure it works well as a product, but a product you can't secure and will you can smell through the lid isn't great. I don't know if it's jut my lid that's the problem, but the packaging seemed to have quite a few flaws.

body: The first time I ever used this product it worked great! So I decided to order it again, and now it lo longer works. It hasn’t caught one fly at all! Not at home nor at work. Disappointed. And it evaporates way quicker than the original!

body: Although generous amount of liquid and super simple to set up, it just isn't doing the job. These are definitely fruitflies & this product isn't working well. After setting next to kitchen sink there's about 10 dead ff in the container, but at least 50 still flying around. Last year when I had fruit flies I microwaved to warm up a bit of apple juice & set that out & the ff loved it, but wanted something easy so tried this Aunt Fannies. I believe the liquid is basically vinegar with some sort of dish soap in it. I can't recommend this product to others.

title: Did not work
body: Ok, so I was so hopeful when I saw the reviews for this. title: Save your money make your own for about 2 CENTS

title: So disappointed! No longer recommend. Seller never responded.
body: FRUIT FLY SEASON IS RAPIDLY APPROACHING AND I'M DETERMINED TO PREVENT LAST SUMMER'S INFESTATION. Update : I contacted the company multiple ways and multiple times. Amazon and the company totally ignored my legitimate complaint. Obviously they don't care about their customers dissatisfaction. It's not about the money - it's about blatant misrepresentation and unethical behavior displayed by both companies. I couldn't even get Amazon to include the "frequently returned" box on the item's page. I bought three bottles of auntie's product on Amazon 6 days ago to replace my DIY liquid attractant of appl cider vinegar +brown sugar +dish detergent. It's been 5 days and can confirm the other negative reviews that the product CAN'T contain the same liquid attractant - the fruit flies feed on the liquid and are not trapped - they can fly away!!! I unintentionally performed a side by side experiment using this WORTHLESS product against my attractant. Both liquids were placed next to separate hanging cylinders of bright yellow sticky fly paper. I actually watched the flies fly from the auntie's product into my liquid. Unlike the auntie product, any flies that were not trapped in my DIY liquid were trapped in the fly paper. After 5 days I had to replace the fly paper adjacent to DIY liquid. in contrast, the 3 bottles of Auntie containing who knows what had A TOTAL OF LESS THAN 20 IN THE BOTTLES AND ABOUT 10 TO 20 TRAPPED BY THE FLY PAPER. I am so angry about wasting money on products from Amazon with good reviews. This product has overall rating of 3.8. But that rating is CUMULATIVE - The much older reviews are generally positive compared to more current negative reviews. I conclude this is due to a change in formulation that neither amazon or the seller made clear. I was so pleased that Good Housekeeping had recommended the best way to eliminates fruit fly infestations in a recent article. The GH panel incorrectly included this product as the only commercially effective liquid attractant since it contained malic acid as part of the formulation. The FRUIT FLY SEASON article made me remember that I had used Aunties successfully a few summers ago and loved their esthetics and effectiveness. I already emailed a request for them to provide evidence of its effectiveness using a recent bottle. I am requesting a refund from this seller based on my results and will update the status with both responses. Meanwhile if you are battling with fruit flies, infestations made worse by the higher temperature (I live in Connecticut) in the Northeast, read below. First understand that you must use the following steps throughout the fruit fly lifecycle (over several weeks so that the original fruit flies are trapped as well as the their progeny hatched from the hundreds of larvae deposited on whatever they fed on. {I am a biochemist and patent attorney so I needed to know what was going on}. Keep in mind for DIY solutions or other traps that you must attract and rid them from escaping. Otherwise you'll have dead flies near and flying around the attractant. A single fruit fly will deposit hundreds of larvae on fruit and vegetables and existing food sources. Follow these steps : 1. Clean all surfaces daily with your typical all purpose cleaner (I use Fantastic with bleach) wherever you find these annoying bugs. For us this is primarily the kitchen in addition to the bathroom and TV room. REMEMBER THEY ARE ATTRACTED TO LIGHT AND 1 FLY WILL DEPOSIT EGGS THAT MATURE IN about 5 to7 DAYS. 2. Unfortunately surface cleaning every 1-2 days is necessary to eliminate flying flies you see and larva that will hatch that you can't. 3. Immediately thoroughly wash all fruit and vegetables (existing or new) and refrigerate. 4. Eliminate All food debris from kitchen counters, microwave, garbage cans, toaster oven, pet water and food bowls, etc. and keep everything covered or washed like used knives, glassware and plates. 5. If you think this is drastic like I did, then you will see an infestation that feels as if those little things won... 6. in the article, Good housekeeping recommended this product as using malic acid which is found in apple cider vinegar. It was part of discussion on using a DIY solution see ingredients above. Any solution must also contain a detergent which causes the flies eating on the attractant liguid to sink in the solution. They can't fly away and begin a new cycle of depositing eggs. At the beginning of the infestation I used the ingredients above along with standing/hanging yellow sticky fly paper I also bought from Amazon. I am very frustrated that I didn't do the research and work upfront instead of wasting money trying to find the non-existent magic bullet all summer!! As much as I love tasty vine ripened tomatoes and other summer fruit and vegetables, it's just not worth it. I think the high temperatures in July throughout the North East as well as nationaly/globally contributed to the problem experienced by me and almost everyone I know.

title: Six Traps Set - One Fly Caught. 80 Bucks Wasted
body: What I liked: It's easy to use. What I disliked: It arrived 2 days late. It doesn't work. It's a spill hazard. It's extremely expensive considering it's vinegar, water, fruit juice and soap. I paid $80 to catch one fly. That about sums it up. We get these fruit flies every year but this year is the worst. I've had the drains cleaned and treated professionally and I'm pouring drain cleaner and fly treatment down the drains daily. I was going to buy the decoy traps that look like an apple. I've used them before and they were great. I couldn't find any in stock, except for one that had bad reviews. Then there was Aunt Fannie's. There's no special formula even though Aunt Fannie's has a patent on their formula. It's different because first, it's not a decorative decoy trap that looks like an apple or mini pumpkin. Aunt Fannie's looks like a spice bottle. When I opened the cap, I expected to see some kind of funnel mechanism on top. That's how the other traps work. The flies are attracted by the sweet formula inside. They slide down the funnel right into the solution and can't get out. Aunt Fannie's just has a wide-mouth opening that can very easily spill. I placed 4 in my kitchen, one in the dining room and one in a bathroom - where the flies congregate as the directions tell you. I watched the flies swarm around the traps and sat back waiting for them to dive in and never check out. They landed on the bottles, walked around, climbed down inside, climbed back out, walked around a little more, then swarmed around. One little fly fell in and couldn't swim. So $80, several days of waiting, then placing these open bottles of liquid all over the place, and I caught one, single fly. Just one. I was convinced to buy this product because I saw so many great reviews. It seemed like a no-brainer when I couldn't find the product I actually wanted. I've never had this happen before. I usually buy stuff with 4 stars or better and when I do, I agree with those reviews. In this case, I was completely wrong and I've wasted time and money.

body: I have never been as disappointed in something from Amazon as I was with this stuff! I had seen them mention it on a TV show. title: Product does not deliver advertised results...
body: I am not sure where they came from (or keep coming from), but I have a small swarm of fruit flies in my kitchen that I have been trying to get rid of for several weeks. I take my trash out daily, have cleaned my kitchen from top to bottom including the drains and trash can, no longer leave fruit (or any other kind of food) out on the counter, and have moved my cat's food and water dishes to another room. I also have tried several DIY natural remedies. Yet the fruit flies persist. I do not want to use an insecticide spray in my home because I have multiple chemical sensitivities. I read about Aunt Fannie's online -- the product got good reviews, so I thought it would be worth a try. The Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch! arrived and I put it out on the counter above where my kitchen trash can is and waited hopefully for it to work its magic. It has been five days and I am still waiting. In five days, Aunt Fannie's has trapped five fruit flies. In the same time period, I have swatted down 29 fruit flies and a sinkful of soapy water that I soaked a couple of pots in for an hour one day trapped seven fruit flies. I am really disappointed in this product -- it was definitely not worth the money. At this point, I am not sure what will work to rid my kitchen or fruit flies, but I feel fairly certain that it will not be Aunt Fannie's.

title: 2 stars because it *does* (sort of) work
body: Otherwise 1. Guys. This overpriced apple cider vinegar with a drip of dish soap. The DIY way works way better. Get a clear up, put a few drops of dish soap in it. Pour in apple cider vinegar so that there is a light "soap lining" over the top. Then cover the glass with well stretched cling wrap. Use a fork to poke s few small holes (easy to get on, hard for them to get out which is a big thing this product misses). The fruit flies smell it and crawl into the holes, ho toward the food-smell and get stuck from the layer of soap. They can't crawl out because of the plastic wrap. Bingo. $1 worth of supplies

title: Don't buy this. Make your own!
body: Well, I got duped by this product. It's mostly my fault. I needed a way to get rid of fruit flies that made their way into my home. I had made my own trap with apple cider vinegar and dish soap, but the vinegar was really bad and stunk up the house. I searched for fruit fly traps and came across this. I gleaned over the description and didn't bother with the reviews (two things I usually never do) and ordered it. It arrived the next day (which is why I bought it) and I opened the package. Much to my surprise and disappointment, it was just a small bottle of apple cider vinegar with soap in it. Man, I felt dumb, but I decided to try it. The cap is a joke. It makes the bottle taller when open and easier to knock over so you can spill it everywhere. Also, it leaks if you close it and don't keep it upright. I poured some into a glass pudding bowl, covered it with plastic wrap and sealed it with a rubber band around the bowl. I poked four 3/8" holes in the wrap, set it out near where the flies are and left for a few minutes. When I came back the flies were all over the bowl. Once they make their way in through the holes they're essentially trapped. You will get the same results with apple cider vinegar and dish soap with this setup (because that's all it is) and over time it'll be cheaper. Don't buy this or any other similar brands. Just make your own trap and save the $8 that I stupidly spent.

title: More still flying around than dying
body: I've used Aunt Fanny's ant spray in the past with good results. So I thought, why not try the fruit fly solution for those pesky pests? Well, here's a good reason: it doesn't work very well. But those fell off the wall and I will return them. So I will buy the ones I should have all along, Terro traps. They worked great and I'm embarrassed that I bothered with anything else. I just wish Terro sold the liquid which how this all began.

title: You can do better
body: I had a THICK CLOUD of fruit flies descend in my kitchen! Researching my options, I found this product & ordered a bottle. While I was desperately awaiting its arrival, however, I fell back on 2 older remedies—beer and apple cider vinegar. Maybe 1/8 of a cup of each of these were poured into separate clean cat food tins with some dish soap for viscosity, then covered with plastic wrap, and punctured with small holes. Once the product arrived, I could easily compare the attraction each liquid possessed. Beer? The winner! Apple cider vinegar? A very close second! Lagging way WAY behind is this product. Granted, it’s got a small number of snagged victims, but nothing like the other two. Save yourself some money. You also get the freebie bonus of finishing off the beer that didn’t get poured into the can!

title: You catch more flies with vinegar...
body: After reading reviews and press for this product, I had high hopes. Unfortunately, the product didn’t quite deliver on my expectations. When the fruit flies first became an issue in my apartment, I tried out a DIY concoction of apple cider vinegar, water, sugar and dish soap. It caught a lot of flies, but not all of them. I ordered this product and put it out in the same room as the DIY solution. Unfortunately, it only caught one fly while my mixture caught 15-20 flies in the same time span. I have continued to leave Fanny’s out, but although the other mix continues to drown flies, this one still only has that one corpse in it. Save your money.

title: Catches some, but not all

It’s just not luring all of them. Ive had it for several weeks. has strong smell initially.

It’s as if you dumped the bait into a mug. The flies mostly sit on the rim then fly off. Perhaps if one could use the bait in a more effective trap, it’d be better, but one generally doesn’t expect to have to buy separate traps at this price. At least it doesn’t smell horrible or like a chem lab; just the homey tang of apple cider vinegar.

title: Didn’t work at all…. Perhaps it was the bug not the product?
body: This is a long story. I bought canned cat food from Amazon, as usual I put it in the cupboard and went on with life. Fast forward, a few days later little bugs started flying around my kitchen, I thought they were fruit flies. For two days I put up with them then bought this. Basically this is apple cider vinegar mixed with sugar. You can make the recipe yourself, which I would do instead of buying this. Now, upon a week after the food was put in the cupboard I opened it and was attacked by these little bombers with wings. The gray of cat food was infested, hundreds with eggs. The can of food in the second tray which was covered with the standard cardboard and outer plastic was split which made a great environment for these little jerks. It took me a week to hand kill these things- thankfully they were slow. Perhaps they were not fruit flies and that is why this product didn’t work. This is not why I am giving it two stars. I am giving it 2 starts because of its application. Once the top is flipped open it is easy to tip over, it is not balanced. The top is completely open because the goal is for the flies to go in for a drink and drown. Well, unless you put this inside a mug it is very easy to accidentally tip over. The smell is nauseating, but that is not the fault of the product, sometime the “medicine” is just awful. I also think it is a little overpriced. $8. For ingredients that would cost at most $.75. I know it is the ease of use and when you are being overtaken by bugs you are willing to pay anything. I am giving it 3 stars because I am indifferent of its effectiveness. I am not sure if these were fruit flies- if they were, then this product didn’t work at all, if they weren’t then I am judging the other aspects of the product: ease of use, quality, cost. Etc. Quality: Nice looking label, The high pungent smell of vinegar is enough to make you gag- so, it is the real deal and not watered down. Ease of use: just peel off the thin protective film and flip open the lid- voila. Cost: I think it’s a little pricey for the ingredients which you could easily make yourself. (They give the recipe online) But, isn’t it easy to press the “buy now” button and have the delivery guy drop at your door 48 hrs later?

title: Meh
body: This stuff worked okay. Maybe some batches are better than others. I bought the two-pack and one seemed to attract a lot of gnats while the other caught very few gnats. I tried switching the placement to see if that helped but it didn’t seem to make much difference. It’s very easy to use-just open the package, flip open the lid and it’s ready to go. I’ve made a similar mixture before with comparable results so I probably won’t buy this again.

title: Maybe Not Fruit Flies
body: The product did not work for me, so I originally posted as one-star. Also, it is not eligible for return, so I was stuck with three jars. I am giving three stars now, because of the communication with Aunt Fannie's. I wrote to them hoping they could help with a return. Kelly wrote back promptly and said the return could be done only through Amazon. But, she was very friendly in e-mail and was sorry the product had not worked. She sent some questions and pictures, wondering if what I have is truly fruit flies. As it turned out and upon further research by me, what I seem to have are drain flies. I have eliminated them with baking soda/vinegar and also baking soda/essential oils. I would recommend to anyone that if FlyPunch is not working, consider another fly besides fruit flies. Also, it is worth writing to the company. I found Aunt Fannie's to be very helpful. Update 12/14/17: I have phorid flies, and they are very difficult to get rid of. My baking soda/vinegar/essential oils invention kept them at bay but didn't truly eliminate them. However, I have found a "trap" by happy accident: ruby red grapefruit juice. The little suckers are actually attracted to an open plastic glass filled with juice. It takes a while for them to figure out that they should jump right in, but they are. I am joyfully seeing dead bodies float. This, after going through frustration trying to kill them. I tried adding a drop or two of dishwashing liquid but am finding they are more attracted to just the juice alone. No ACV, orange juice, beer, or red wine for my visitors. Ruby red grapefruit juice. Who knew.

I did notice a significant decrease in the number of small flying insects in 7-10 days; just not an immediate impact. Cats do not like the vinegar smell & leave it alone wherever you put it (off the floor).

Does it work? Yes. Do I still have the same type of flies that I had before? Yes, yes I do. Have I tried moving it around where I see flies? Yes, I have. If I had to guess I have 6 flies/gnats, and the bottle has 3 of them. So I gave it a 3/5 rating for getting me 50% of the flies.

title: Total waste of money in my case
body: I have been battling fruit flies in my kitchen for a while. I've tried several methods including fly strips as well as multiple homemade traps using differing methods (mason jar with apple cider vinegar & dish soap, wine bottles with a bit of wine left, mason jars with apple cider vinegar *and* rotting fruit with saran wrap & holes poked, jars with paper funnel, etc.) I've even heated the apple cider vinegar before setting out the traps to produce an aroma of the fermenting vinegar/fruit. I had high hopes for this product but it literally only caught 1 or 2 fruit flies. I caught many more with just regular fly strips that catch them by chance. I left this product in two separate places in my kitchen for over a week and the fruit flies ignored it completely. Total waste of money in my case. I got rid of my fruit flies by actively spraying them with a spray bottle filled with dish soap & water, fly strips, and pouring boiling water down the drain every day (and being diligent about not leaving food crumbs out). Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch did not help at all and was a waste of money in my case. The fruit flies I had completely ignored this product (which smells like it is simply apple cider vinegar anyway).

title: An expensive version of a cheap home remedy that doesn't work
body: I probably should have researched the product a bit more before buying it. After opening it it became very obvious from the smell and look what it was. It's literally just a bottle of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of soap. It even says so in the ingredient list "vinegar, water, ethyl lactate(aka soap)". To be fair it does kind of say that in the description so that's on me. Does it work? - About as well as apple cider vin and soap does (because that's what this product is). I've heard of this working for others so that's what I tried before buying this. For me I caught about 5 flies with my home made stuff and 3 with this product. My other home made trap was a bottle with a small amount of fruit juice and sealed with some plastic wrap with a few small holes. That has caught around 50. Still have an infestation. This, along with the home made stuff, will make the whole area smell of vinegar. If you really want to try this method then just make it yourself for half the cost. Most people have acv and soap laying around anyways. And if it doesn't work then at least you'll have left over soap you can use to clean and acv you can cook with.

From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. title: Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch! Fruit Fly Trap ...
body: I have been battling fruit flies for 2 weeks! Between the produce I buy and my fruit flavored vape juice they have been relentless. I just received one of these today along with a 2 pack of Terro brand "Peaches". I set all three out in my house. One Terro and this product in kitchen and one Terro in my den. The Aunt Fannie's product has eliminated more flies than the two Terro peaches combined so far (less than 24 hours). Update: You can lead a fly to a lure, but you can't make the fly jump in. I ended up finding a chemical product called PT Alpine that eliminated all the flies in my home in 48 hours.

title: Fruit Fly Trap
body: We all of a sudden had a huge amount of fruit flys in our kitchen and bathroom areas. Tried all the home made remedies we could think of and nothing seemed to work. I bought Aunt Fannies Fruit Fly Killer from Amazon and was hoping to get rid of them all. Much to our disappointment, it did not work as well as we had hoped. It did trap a few flies, but not any better than the home made remedies we tried. We are still battling with them. We even bough a spray by RAID it does kill them but not all of them. Don't know where they are coming from or how to get rid of them

title: So it did work….
body: But only for about a week. Honestly this is just apple cider vinegar in a spice container. You could make it yourself if you just buy vinegar and dawn soap.

title: There are better products on the market.
body: Okay so I managed to get some fruit flies the first few days, but not all. Obviously the more you have, the better chance you will get at getting rid of fruit flies. I would consider it mildly effective at best though. And because the lid opens up wide without any sort of barrier, I have unfortunately knocked it over several times and had to clean up a stinky mix of smelly vinegar and dead bugs. After the initial effectiveness wore off, no more flies are taking the bait--I still have tons of flies everywhere. I think you're better off investing in a better product.

title: Works as well as vinegar and dish soap.
body: Works as well as dish soap and apple cidar vinegar or regular white vinegar. More expensive than the mentioned method. The container is cool but you could buy one for cheap. Good option is you do not wish to out the ingredients together yourself and pour into a container. I caught two fruit flies with it, my vinegar and dish soap caught three over a 24 hour period. Could be location of containers. I ended up swatting about 10 of them myself. So get a gooe fly swatter. The flies will land in areas and you can see them and crush their souls.

title: Didn’t Work as fast as I thought it would
body: I liked how easy it was to use, but it took awhile for the flies to get attracted to it, and the smell was a very strong vinegar smell.

title: Works great but wasn’t packaged well
body: These have historically worked great for me, but this is my first time ordering them from Amazon. Both had burst open and leaked all throughout the packaging causing a sticky mess.

title: kinda works?
body: Bought this for some fruit flies we had, had it opened in my room for about 4 days and in that time it caught 2 flies. It's nice because it requires very zero effort but in the same amount of time, I manually squashed maybe 2 or 3 by myself. I don't think the flies were especially attracted to it, but perhaps the unlucky ones who happen to stumble across will get caught. I ended up closing the jar and putting it away because the smell was bothering me more than it was attracting/catching the flies.

title: Only for fruit flies
body: My office has a problem with drain gnats. I thought I would give this a try even though the description says it's specifically designed only for fruit flies. Well they weren't lying. Not a single gnat went in this bottle. They circle it and land right next to it but do not go in. Also, this thing just contains apple cider vinegar and a little soap. You could use an empty spice container and make the same thing at home.

title: Impressed by the Reviews but Disappointed by the Results
body: I have been needing a fruit fly trap desperately and had seen this was one of the top rated products. I had been hoping it’s simple design would be all there was so I left it adjacent to our sink and garbage can (a hotspot) and let it be. Two weeks later, there are only 3 measly flies down at the bottom compared to other pictures I’ve seen where there are dozens gathered down there. I’ve noticed the flies don’t actually go down in the bottle and mostly walk around the outer rim before flying off. Maybe mine are just too smart...

title: Worked ok
body: It’s an ok product caught some fruit flys not all of them and it just smells like vinegar and could be made at home

title: Stinky product
body: Omg, this stuff smells so bad! I mean maybe that’s the point to attract the bugs, but I couldn’t stand to be in the same room as an open container of this. For the most part I left it open at night and then lit a candle to get rid of the smell the next morning. To make matters worse, I ended up accidentally knocking over mine.. dead bug juice everywhere. It does work, but not enough for me to want to buy this product again.

title: Worked decent after awhile
body: Like a lot of reviews have mentioned, I opened this thing up with a decent number of fruit flies around and was having seemingly no success. I went ahead and left it in position near my trash can and after a few days it finally started to catch them. Not sure if they needed time to warm up to it or what, but it works decent these days for a relatively cheap product that doesn't stink up the place TOO bad.

title: Doesn’t seem to attract fruit flies
body: Love ease of use, but out of all the different types of traps we set out, these were the only ones that barely attracted a single fruit fly. The ones that work the best are the ones shaped like little red apples with lots of holes in the top. Those are now full of dead fruit flies, but the Aunt fannies fly punch traps have only one fruit fly trapped out of all four of the traps that we set out.

title: Not effective
body: It as effective as I would have liked!

title: Gnats
body: The product works okay but not as good as I expected.

title: Moderately effective
body: Liked the dead fruit flies! Prefer not having another open liquid container on my kitchen sink, but workable if careful. Has time-limited effectiveness. DOES attract the little buggers but dont expect immediate results. Not the wayvm it's intended to work.

title: Im not sure...
body: So I will say the product works because it did capture a lot of flies after a while. I guess my main concern was that It had to sit on the counter for a long time before anything really started to happen. Im kind of on the fence about ordering again because of that fact. other than that, the product was great, didn't have a unpleasant smell and arrived very quickly.

title: Worked better when there were A LOT of fruit flies
body: Originally this product worked as well as if I'd just put a cup of water on the counter. In over a couple of days since opening it, it was put to use near the source of the problem, and it lured/killed 2 fruit flies while the rest continued to fly around freely in the kitchen. Disappointed 😕 but once I put it around a higher concentration of flies, it lured more. It didn't work well when there were only 5-10 flies.

title: Not The Best Product For Catching Fruit Flies
body: Having a Bearded Dragon and Guinea Pigs as well as breeding my own meal worms and super worms for my Bearded Dragon and to sell we tend to get a lot of fruit flies. I bought a 6-pack but unfortunately they have not really been successful in catching the fruit flies. There have been an average of about five in each bottle. It is easy and convenient but not doing the job as we had hoped.

title: Not effective. the "apple" fruit fly traps work better
body: thought they were expensive apple cider vinegar..

title: Not worth it
body: So so. It smells like vinegar mostly and there’s no way to prevent a spill if it’s open. The flies land on the side a lot. The second one I ordered didn’t work at all. Like they got immune to it or something. Orange juice did the trick in a fraction of the time so save your money.

title: Doesn’t kill them, only attracts them.
body: This doesn't work, it attracts more fruit flies but does not kill them. I used it for more then 2 months and hasn't killed one… I have a lot more flies then before actually.

title: Save your money.
body: Ineffective -- we recently had an issue with fruit flies and this product didn't do its job. Better luck with homemade solution of water, vinegar, and dish soap. Also found sticky traps worked.

title: Fruit Flies Roundly Ignored this substance.
body: Have many fruit flies. Only one was drawn to this solution. Also, one of two bottles leaked all over the packaging. Returned after let it sit there on my counter tempting none of the fruit flies.

title: Don’t buy if you love your life!
body: Do not buy this! I repeat! Do not buy this! Within 10 minutes your house will be full of something that you cannot put your finger on other than grasping for fresh air and trying not to meet your maker. Someone decided that putting some sort of mix of ether, apple cider vinegar and some concoction of liquid from the pits of hell together and put it in a bottle said to be safe for home use and thought that was a good idea. 10/10 do not recommend! Just let the fruit flies dance!

title: Total waste of money in my case
body: I have been battling fruit flies in my kitchen for a while. I've tried several methods including fly strips as well as multiple homemade traps using differing methods (mason jar with apple cider vinegar & dish soap, wine bottles with a bit of wine left, mason jars with apple cider vinegar *and* rotting fruit with saran wrap & holes poked, jars with paper funnel, etc.) I've even heated the apple cider vinegar before setting out the traps to produce an aroma of the fermenting vinegar/fruit. I had high hopes for this product but it literally only caught 1 or 2 fruit flies. I caught many more with just regular fly strips that catch them by chance. I left this product in two separate places in my kitchen for over a week and the fruit flies ignored it completely. Total waste of money in my case. I got rid of my fruit flies by actively spraying them with a spray bottle filled with dish soap & water, fly strips, and pouring boiling water down the drain every day (and being diligent about not leaving food crumbs out). Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch did not help at all and was a waste of money in my case. The fruit flies I had completely ignored this product (which smells like it is simply apple cider vinegar anyway).

title: An expensive version of a cheap home remedy that doesn't work
body: I probably should have researched the product a bit more before buying it. After opening it it became very obvious from the smell and look what it was. It's literally just a bottle of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of soap. It even says so in the ingredient list "vinegar, water, ethyl lactate(aka soap)". To be fair it does kind of say that in the description so that's on me. Does it work? - About as well as apple cider vin and soap does (because that's what this product is). I've heard of this working for others so that's what I tried before buying this. For me I caught about 5 flies with my home made stuff and 3 with this product. My other home made trap was a bottle with a small amount of fruit juice and sealed with some plastic wrap with a few small holes. That has caught around 50. Still have an infestation. This, along with the home made stuff, will make the whole area smell of vinegar. If you really want to try this method then just make it yourself for half the cost. Most people have acv and soap laying around anyways. And if it doesn't work then at least you'll have left over soap you can use to clean and acv you can cook with.

title: Ineffective and malodorous
body: I did not expect to open the bottle and find that it was a wide-open design and thus easily spillable. I have pets (including a very inquisitive and ungraceful cat), so I can't put it in certain places. I did try to put one in the kitchen but a tiny spider on the windowsill nearby is catching more fruit flies than this trap. The smell of vinegar is quite strong and not pleasant, and so far the fly trap hasn't caught a single obnoxious flying anything.

title: Do not recommend
body: This has been put on my counter for over a day. There is not a single fruit fly in it. Definitely would not recommend. Terro traps are much more effective.

title: Very disappointed
body: I finally received this item after a lengthy shipping period. Both bottles had the caps on wrong and all of the liquid was gone, the packaging is wet and smells like the product. Probably left a trail of fruit fly fluid the whole way.

title: Well it didn’t work, also leaked out before I got it…
body: When I say this was the biggest disappointment I have come across in along time, I mean it. Now this worked for my friend and was recommended to me so I thought, trusted review from a trusted person so why not. Yeah no, smell is much stronger than regular soap and apple cider vinegar but I was willing to smell( it in a completely different room mind you) as long as it worked. Received the product and both bottles were leaking all over the Amazon package… oh well moving on. Left it out for a couple of days and didn’t catch one bug, not a gnat, not a fruit fly, only attention it caught was mine cause that smell was STRONG. You would have better luck just making a concoction yourself or buying a big light for gnats and fruit flies- that’s what I did when I returned this. Would not recommend to anyone but my enemy.

title: Not worth it for the price
body: I just don’t like it

title: Good concept but not great results
body: Still waiting. One fruit fly caught. My resolution - take caution using - pouring hot water from the tea kettle down all drains - it eradicates living fruit flies and the eggs if they have laid any in your drains. Haven't seen a bug since! To be sure, I have treated every night before bedtime for 4 days. Total success!

title: Sadness and despair
body: One can came empty. Amazon won’t respond I can’t get the seller to respond. So I pours half the liquid from one into the other and set them out. It’s been two days not a single fruit fly. :( I had high hopes but it really doesn’t work for me.

title: Stinks
body: Stinks and leaking. I don’t know why I expected it to have a way too keep the bugs in, like you do when you set up a home made one. But there’s no way to trap them in.

title: Works BUT see the photos attached and you decide
body: The FlyPunch works, BUT,... I had much better luck with a simple household product that didn’t cost me but a few pennies. Both traps were set at the same time 48-52 hours ago. FlyPunch and a bowl of apple cider Venegar with 2-3 drops of dish soap stirred in. Traps were set 3-4 inches apart on the kitchen window. Pictures attached that shows a massive difference between the 2 traps. I was able to count 8 fruit flies in the FlyPunch and far too many to count in the apple cider vinegar mix Can’t say if the FlyPunch would have worked better with the cling wrap, often saw fruit flies sitting on the rim but not too many died. I simply followed the directions on the bottle and did the same with the apple cider trap I googled. 🤷🏽♂️ Left for Thanksgiving and forgot to throw out the bananas, and Shazam,... lots of fruit flies when we returned. 48-52 hours later 99% are gone. You decide which trap worked better.

title: Didn’t work!!
body: Had high hopes this product would work… But… Not one fruit fly took the bate.. very disappointed!

title: Didn't work for me
body: I bought this product because I began to have fruit flies in my apartment. I wanted something easy, something that didn't require much work, so I thought this would be perfect. Just open and forget it. Well after almost two weeks it only caught two fruit flies, just TWO. I was pretty disappointed. I ended up just buying one of those electrical fan things that have a light that are made to trap fruit flies via the fan down onto a glue board. I ran this for two weeks and caught almost 60! So this fan thing worked way better than this liquid. And to top it off, no refunds are allowed. Very shady in my opinion. If my fan trap caught 60 and this liquid caught 2, then it obviously if faulty and I should have the option to get my money back. Do not waste your money on this product.

title: Toxic. Misleading Amazon description.
body: Sorry I ordered this and it will be going down the drain. The description says it’s “plant-based” and “safe around food”. But the label on the product contains several warnings, including to wear rubber gloves when handling and what to do if it gets on your skin. When it’s set up for use it’s an open bottle, just waiting to tip over. It contains Ethyl Lactate: “Ethyl lactate can be harmful if inhaled or absorbed through the skin. Prolonged contact can irritate the skin and eyes, and breathing it in can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, and passing out. Ethyl lactate is flammable and can cause serious or permanent injury”

title: A 100% useless product
body: Completely useless against gnats (fruit flies)...or any other fly infestation. A total BS product. Don't be fooled!

title: Bad product
body: Does not work. The flies aren’t attracted to the trap.

title: Terrible!
body: I bought two of these and left them out for three weeks. Neither caught a single fruit fly/gnat. I cannot believe I wasted $16 on these. I do not understand how anyone gave these good reviews! If I could give 5 negative stars, I would.

title: So disappointing
body: I have been struggling with fruit flies for a few weeks now and I have been trying every trick in the book. I did some research and heard about these and thought oh finally something easy to help with these annoying things. I have had them out for two days now and nothing….it attracts the fruit flys but they don’t go inside and if they do they come right back out. I thought I would try dumping some of it into a shallow plate but that did not work, I tried putting it in a bowl and that does not work either. I had got these little apple looking things prior and they worked pretty well so I just ordered a bunch of those alone with a drain killer to pour down my kitchen drain and hopefully soon I won’t have an issue anymore. But all in all I would not recommend these.

title: Not worth it
body: Purchased this product, and was very excited to use it since I have a pesky fruit fly problem. The bottles came broken. Some of the contents spilled into the packaging. Contacted customer support from the dealer and they do not do refunds since I bought through Amazon. Decided to use the product anyway, from what I had. I’ve had it open for 3 days now. It has caught one fly. All the other flies just fly around it. Product did not work for me. Don’t waste your money.

title: It hasn't caught a single fly...
body: When we open the back door, we've discovered flies congregating by the door, and invariably, at least a couple of flies fly in the door. (We have to go in and out a lot to walk dogs). I got one of those battery-operated fly eliminators that look like a tennis racket, thinking I could get them right at the door, but I'm not fast enough. We tried sticky fly paper, which works quite well, but it isn't attractive. I thought we'd give this a try. In four days, it hasn't attracted a single fly. There is nothing in containers. I got six. I put two out. I'm very disappointed because these containers sure look better than fly paper. I will update if there's any change but so far, not one fly...

title: Not worth buying
body: This product doesn’t do much if you’re looking at drastically improving a gnat infestation. Get a drain cleaner instead. This is too gentle and doesn’t do much. Save your money. I wish I could return this lol

title: Does not work at all!
body: We had a lot of fruit flies upon returning from vacation. We tried these traps and caught only two flies with them in two weeks! The jars do not have any way to trap the flies, the lid is wide open, and this is a flaw of design. If the lid had smaller holes in it, the flies would get trapped in there. The flies fly into these traps and do not stay there--whatever is in it does not attract or kill them. We got rid of our fruit flies using yellow sticky glue traps and other liquid fruit fly traps that have a better attractant and design to keep the flies trapped. And also good old-fashioned home-made vinegar, water, dish soap traps helped--with a dash of apple-cider vinegar as attractant or small piece of fruit in it.

title: Don't bother
body: Strong vinegar smell, but tolerable. After 2 months, only 6 fruit flies. My leftover glass of wine works much better. Leave a small bowl of wine or juice overnight. Much more effective.

title: Useless
body: Literally did nothing. Left it out for 5 days and 0 flies went in. Waste of money

title: It didn't work this time, formula change?
body: Unlike the same product we purchased previously that worked really well, these two bottles were completely ineffective. Not a single fruit fly was caught, while my used wine glasses attracted many. I am not sure if there was any formula changes, but these simply didn’t work at all.

title: Didn't work for me AT ALL
body: I have several fruit flies around the spyder plants in my kitchen (and near a counter at the other end of the kitchen where I have bananas hanging). I bought this with high hopes... but no go. Initially I opened the bottle, placed it between two plants and gave it a few days. Nothing. I then poured it into four small shallow open containers and placed three around all the plants and one near the bananas. Five days later, only 1 fruit fly ended up in any of the containers (I think it got in there by accident & drowned). I can say that after all this time, the smell of apple cider is still very strong. From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. I had hoped this would have some sort attractant I didn't know about and would work, but could have saved my money and gone back to a plain old cider vinegar & dishsoap mix (which gave me the same result but was much cheaper).

title: Caught three flies only. Put your investment elsewhere.
body: I paid almost $8 to catch three flies. My cat would have done a better job. Basically useless did absolutely nothing to solve my problem. I would be investing in something else.

title: Total failure
body: sadly they do not work - don't know why but I was hoping this took care of my problem but not happening - going back to my local hardware store to get the ones that have worked in the past and these are going back to Amazon

title: Junk
body: Don’t waste your money! Not only is this nothing more than vinegar, it is a poor design. The top is just wide open. You have to have small holes so the fruit flies can get in but not out! They were all just hanging out on the popped top diving in for a slurp of vinegar and then resting back on the top. I had more success with a small jar of vinegar with cling wrap poked with a toothpick! China is dumping their junk and Amazon is selling it to us!

title: Doesn’t work.
body: Initially I had high hope for this based on what others were saying. Unfortunately these were a huge let down for me. The design is clumsy at best and is a spill waiting to happen, It’s just a wide open bottle. I have left one out for over a week now where I have an abundance of fruit flies. Not a single fly in it, they’re not even interested in these. Save your money and find a working product.

title: Save Your $ & Make A Trap From A Old Water Bottle & Vinegar!
body: A homemade trap from an old water bottle & vinegar with a few drops of soap works better than this any day! This simply doesn't work. The reviewers that say it does must have some bad infestations or something as I've had this in various locations for several weeks and not ONE fruit fly was captured! I even added some foil over the top and poked a few holes as some suggested and it still is a miserable failure!

title: Odd bottle
body: The bottle is odd designed, unprofessional, unpractical.

title: Don’t waste your money
body: Ineffective, and will not get the job done. You could probably make something better on your own.

title: Ridiculous
body: Do not waste your time nor your money. Zero effectiveness. Nothing else needs to be stated. Have a nice day.

title: Just ACV! Biggest waste of money
body: Biggest rip off ever. This item is literally a plastic spice jar of apple cider vinegar, you could make this for 50 cents in less time it would take to order this with items in your kitchen. Actually unreal that i just paid $8 for this, should have read the ingredients. Was specifically trying to not use apple cider vinegar because it stinks. DO NOT BUY! It doesn’t work very well.

title: Didn't work- not a single fly
body: We've been having a massive Fruit Fly issue and been trying everything we could to get it under control. I had high hopes for these but we've had two of them open for a week now and not a single Fruit fly has gone for these. We've moved them around to different areas of our pantry and kitchen and nothing. We've had better luck with homemade traps using dish soap w/ red wine or cider vinegar. They still aren't managing the situation but at least SOME dead flies have resulted from those.

title: Didn’t work at all
body: I bought a two pack of these….they both collectively caught three gnats. Mind you, I’m having an infestation right now. My own home made ACV and sugar water with dawn dish soap worked way better.

title: Charging for 12 bottles and sending just 1 bottle
body: Ordered the 12 pack for $80 and received just one bottle. Requested a replacement and received one bottle instead of 12 again despite a charge for a 12 pack

title: Don’t waste your time or money!!
body: This was an absolute freaking waste of money. I am so irritated because it was one of those products that really stood out to me, like no way thousands of people are being dishonest and rating it highly consistently. Boy was I wrong. So, I have a summer time issue with fruit flies (due to fruit). Could not get rid of them for anything. I used the katchy, stem spray, and this product. I had my home PROFESSIONALLY cleaned, opened one of these jars, and left for a 2-week vacation. I just knew I would be coming back to a fruit fly free home thanks to this product working it’s magic. No such luck. I’ll stop there, but just take it from me. It is a waste of money, so don’t get your hopes up.

title: Don’t waist your money!!!
body: If I can give zero stars, I would, but it makes me pick at least one. Total waste of money. I’ve worked in the bar industry for years, I’ve seen barflies congregate around the alcohol for years. I bought this product because it said it was specifically formulated for barflies. At the three days only two barflies were caught in the syrup. I decided to buy another product and filled the bottom cup portion with Jim Bean. Within an hour, there was over a dozen flies caught in the trap. Don’t waste your money. This product does not work.

title: sent an open product
body: we were sent a product that was open, spilled all over the bag and one of the containers was missing half the liquid

title: Disappointed
body: I was having an awful problem with fruit flies in the kitchen and dining room. I read about using apple cider vinegar and water or, even better, Flypunch. I had apple cider vinegar on hand so I tried it first and ordered Flypunch on the same day. After two days of using the apple cider vinegar 95% of the fruit flies were gone. The Flypunch arrived and I figured it would clear up the remaining 5%. That was not the case. After three days of using only the Flypunch, two bottles, the fruit flies were back. I pulled out the apple cider vinegar and the next morning the flies were gone. If you want to get rid of fruit flies first try the apple cider vinegar.

title: Aunt Fannies No Catch Punch
body: This product did not work for me! I have had it out for about a week. There were only two fruit flies captured. I purchased another product which seems to have caught the ones that Aunt Fannies fly punch didn't catch. I absolutely wasted my money.

title: More wasted money
body: I purchased Aunt Fannie's fly punch fruit fly trap based on all of the encouraging reviews. More wasted money! It smelled just like vinegar when I opened it and left it out for quite a few days with quite a few fruit flies .They were not interested! I have a picture of the open container of the fly punch next to a tuna fish can filled with regular apple cider vinegar and a few pieces of old fruit. Regular apple cider vinegar caught more fruit flies compared to the fly punch which caught none.

title: Boo..
body: Hasn't caught anything!! It ended up getting knocked over... what a mess!! It smells like vinegar. My son found a DIY recipe online and it's only caught a few but it was free!! I did a thorough cleaning with bleach on counters, floors, and cabinets and it's adequate a noticeable difference for today anyway!! Save your money... or throw it away but don't give it to these people!!

title: Ease of use
body: When I got my product one bottle the lid was loose and had leaked all out in package . So didn’t even get to use it. We shall see if it really works as of now not sure. Don’t like the lid has to be completely open should have some kind of guard where the liquids won’t leak out if tipped over

title: seems my used wine glasses that sit on the counter overnite get more attention from the fruit flys
body: not what i expected . takes quite a while to attract the fruit flys

title: It works better for me than home-made.
body: A lot of people are upset that this is basically just the home remedy of apple cider vinegar and soap. And yeah, it is, but I’m catching way more of the flies with this than the home brew, so Aunt Fannie’s doing something right. I wish it was a little more enclosed though, because the open mouth with the unwieldy flip top is begging for it to get tipped over and spill.

title: Would try again
body: I love aunt fannies products, this one just did not work for the little flies in my house. I’ve done everything and they won’t go away, so it may not be this products fault.

title: Kill nets
body: Did not kill the fruit flys

title: Worked
body: Although it worked,it didn’t perform as I hoped

title: Not great
body: The flies don't go in. Doesn't work.

title: It's trying to work
body: It attracts the flies, but the lip is perfect for them to have a little snack and not fall in. I watched one fly in yesterday so I know it works. I've removed the lid to see if that is the problem. You could probably make one of these yourself if you wanted to save like 4 bucks considering what you need to make this included.

title: Not sure what it supposed to do 🤔
body: So to be honest. I'm really not sure what it is supposed to do. According to the description it should trap the fruit fly but it didn't trap even one but it repelled them where I don't have any in my house anymore which the goal. So I'm happy with it. It did deliver what I paid for even though it is the opposite outcome🤪🤪

title: cider vinegar works just as well and is cheaper
body: We went on vacation and forgot to take out the trash so when we returned home the house was full of fruit flies. I set out little dishes of cider vinegar with a drop of dish soap to get rid of them but they were not disappearing fast enough so I purchased this to see if it would work quicker. It looks and smells just like the cider vinegar and only worked about as well. There were no more bugs in this than in the other home remedies I used so it was really a waste of money to buy it when it didn't work any better.

title: Nice packaging, but doesn’t work.
body: I’m sorry, I thought this cute little bottle with the peculiar odor would be the end of my fruit fly problem. Nope. A few of the little buggers have flown in, but not enough to make a difference. I’m also afraid I’m going to knock it over. Uggh. No re-buy for this product.

title: Catching fruit flys
body: Did not work right away, over a few days noticed flys in liquid, but did not work quickly

title: Fruit Flies do like it
body: Tt worked instantly, fruit flies hovering over it and dove into the liquid... but it slowed down considerably. It could be that I got a fair amount of them, not sure. I still see one or two/three, etc buzzing around. I've only had this for a week....so I'll try to update this review. Smells like apple cider vinegar, so if that's what is in this, you could make a home remedy

title: Attracts flies.
body: It does attract flies. The cost per volume seems high.

title: It works but not for a large infestation
body: This product is okay but I would highly recommend one of the products you pour into the sink and let sit overnight.

title: These bugs are literally mocking me
body: I have little knats in my house and I thought maybe I'd leave the formulating of these traps up to the pros. They have been out now for almost 24 hours, not 1 big captured. Update. I think I have a combined 18 dead. So... I take it back... It does work.

title: Make Your Own For a Lower Price
body: It's essentially apple cider vinegar with soap- you could make something like the product by yourself and for way less money. As another reviewer pointed out, the bait liquid itself will probably drown some fruit flies but to really maximize the number of fruit flies it kills, you need to stick some doubled sided sticky fly traps into the bottle. If you do this, you'll be amazed and disgusted by how much fruit flies have been lurking around your home.

title: Package leaks
body: Package leaks and the fluid was all over the inside of it and it smells pretty bad so that's my review

title: Not Worth It
body: I didn't look closely at the photos and assumed the lid had small holes in it, but it's just a wide open lid. You're better off pouring some cheap apple cider vinegar and dish soap in an old cup of your own. I've noticed that this method of catching fruit flies works best when you use a paper funnel or poke holes in plastic wrap, to trap them once they're lured in. I caught more doing that than I did with this wide open on my counter.

title: Use apple cider vinegar instead
body: Save yourself a few bucks and use apple cider vinegar, the cheap stuff, because that's basically all this product is, with a couple of other things thrown in that you don't really need. I've been using the same container and have just been adding some vinegar to it as needed, but you can use any container you have available. I haven't noticed any difference in their product vs. the apple cider vinegar. It still attracts them into the bottle and there they stay, in the liquid, until you dump it out and refresh it.

title: Probably useless!
body: I tried this product Because i was desperate to get rid of fruit flies. It’s my nderstanding that the that the flies would be attracted to it, enter the bottle and die. If I’m correct, the product was useless,as it did not draw a single fly into it, despite my having left it open on my kitchen counter for 4 days. It just so happens that the infestation had significantly improved by the time I received and set the bottle out, and the flies were actually almost gone by the end of the 4 days, so IF the product works just by sitting open and on the counter, it MAY be that the product did work. At this time I’m just trying to be fair and offer the seller the benefit of the doubt; however, I cannot, now give the product more than one star. I invite the seller to clarify the situation, especially if the product does not need to draw the flies into it for it to work. Also, however, the odor emitted from the jar is so strong and pervasive that it made me nauseous and I doubt I could have tolerated it much longer.
