title: It does not work !
body: I bought this brought June 2025. I opened the lid and placed it on the kitchen counter next to the fruit bowl. I let it sit there in disturbed until September 3, 2025, absolutely nothing happened to the flying fruit flies. The fruit flies ignored the bottle all together! Do not waste your money !

title: No longer effective, change in formula?
body: UPDATED REVIEW: Two years ago my apartment has very annoying fruit flies - I lived in a house of four girls, with all of our bananas and avocados and tomatoes, etc, that made it impossible to live produce free for long enough to make the bugs go away. I bought this product, and within days there were over 15 fruit flies that it had gotten rid of. I bought more, and our fruit fly problem went away and stayed away. This year, with the summer heat and plethora of summer fruit, the fruit flies are back. And this time, after buying 5 of these liquid traps, none of them are working. I even see fruit flies flying immediately next to the traps, but after 4 weeks of hoping they would start working again they are not, and I am thoroughly disappointed. The company must have changed their formula for this drastic of a decline in its effectiveness.

body: This doesn't work, it attracts more fruit flies but does not kill them. I used it for more then 2 months and hasn't killed one… I have a lot more flies then before actually.

title: Save your money.
body: Ineffective -- we recently had an issue with fruit flies and this product didn't do its job. Better luck with homemade solution of water, vinegar, and dish soap. Also found sticky traps worked.

title: Fruit Flies Roundly Ignored this substance.
body: Have many fruit flies. Only one was drawn to this solution. Also, one of two bottles leaked all over the packaging. Returned after let it sit there on my counter tempting none of the fruit flies.

title: Don’t buy if you love your life!
body: Do not buy this! I repeat! Do not buy this! Within 10 minutes your house will be full of something that you cannot put your finger on other than grasping for fresh air and trying not to meet your maker. Someone decided that putting some sort of mix of ether, apple cider vinegar and some concoction of liquid from the pits of hell together and put it in a bottle said to be safe for home use and thought that was a good idea. 10/10 do not recommend! Just let the fruit flies dance!

title: Total waste of money in my case
body: I have been battling fruit flies in my kitchen for a while. I've tried several methods including fly strips as well as multiple homemade traps using differing methods (mason jar with apple cider vinegar & dish soap, wine bottles with a bit of wine left, mason jars with apple cider vinegar *and* rotting fruit with saran wrap & holes poked, jars with paper funnel, etc.) I've even heated the apple cider vinegar before setting out the traps to produce an aroma of the fermenting vinegar/fruit. I had high hopes for this product but it literally only caught 1 or 2 fruit flies. I caught many more with just regular fly strips that catch them by chance. I left this product in two separate places in my kitchen for over a week and the fruit flies ignored it completely. Total waste of money in my case. I got rid of my fruit flies by actively spraying them with a spray bottle filled with dish soap & water, fly strips, and pouring boiling water down the drain every day (and being diligent about not leaving food crumbs out). Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch did not help at all and was a waste of money in my case. The fruit flies I had completely ignored this product (which smells like it is simply apple cider vinegar anyway).

title: An expensive version of a cheap home remedy that doesn't work
body: I probably should have researched the product a bit more before buying it. After opening it it became very obvious from the smell and look what it was. It's literally just a bottle of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of soap. It even says so in the ingredient list "vinegar, water, ethyl lactate(aka soap)". To be fair it does kind of say that in the description so that's on me. Does it work? - About as well as apple cider vin and soap does (because that's what this product is). I've heard of this working for others so that's what I tried before buying this. For me I caught about 5 flies with my home made stuff and 3 with this product. My other home made trap was a bottle with a small amount of fruit juice and sealed with some plastic wrap with a few small holes. That has caught around 50. Still have an infestation. This, along with the home made stuff, will make the whole area smell of vinegar. If you really want to try this method then just make it yourself for half the cost. Most people have acv and soap laying around anyways. And if it doesn't work then at least you'll have left over soap you can use to clean and acv you can cook with.

title: Ineffective and malodorous
body: I did not expect to open the bottle and find that it was a wide-open design and thus easily spillable. I have pets (including a very inquisitive and ungraceful cat), so I can't put it in certain places. I did try to put one in the kitchen but a tiny spider on the windowsill nearby is catching more fruit flies than this trap. The smell of vinegar is quite strong and not pleasant, and so far the fly trap hasn't caught a single obnoxious flying anything.

title: Do not recommend
body: This has been put on my counter for over a day. There is not a single fruit fly in it. Definitely would not recommend. Terro traps are much more effective.

title: Very disappointed
body: I finally received this item after a lengthy shipping period. Both bottles had the caps on wrong and all of the liquid was gone, the packaging is wet and smells like the product. Probably left a trail of fruit fly fluid the whole way.

title: Didn't work for me AT ALL
body: I have several fruit flies around the spyder plants in my kitchen (and near a counter at the other end of the kitchen where I have bananas hanging). I bought this with high hopes... but no go. Initially I opened the bottle, placed it between two plants and gave it a few days. Nothing. I then poured it into four small shallow open containers and placed three around all the plants and one near the bananas. Five days later, only 1 fruit fly ended up in any of the containers (I think it got in there by accident & drowned). I can say that after all this time, the smell of apple cider is still very strong. From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. I had hoped this would have some sort attractant I didn't know about and would work, but could have saved my money and gone back to a plain old cider vinegar & dishsoap mix (which gave me the same result but was much cheaper).

title: Caught three flies only. Put your investment elsewhere.
body: I paid almost $8 to catch three flies. My cat would have done a better job. Basically useless did absolutely nothing to solve my problem. I would be investing in something else.

title: Total failure
body: sadly they do not work - don't know why but I was hoping this took care of my problem but not happening - going back to my local hardware store to get the ones that have worked in the past and these are going back to Amazon

title: Junk
body: Don’t waste your money! Not only is this nothing more than vinegar, it is a poor design. The top is just wide open. You have to have small holes so the fruit flies can get in but not out! They were all just hanging out on the popped top diving in for a slurp of vinegar and then resting back on the top. I had more success with a small jar of vinegar with cling wrap poked with a toothpick! China is dumping their junk and Amazon is selling it to us!

title: Doesn’t work.
body: Initially I had high hope for this based on what others were saying. Unfortunately these were a huge let down for me. The design is clumsy at best and is a spill waiting to happen, It’s just a wide open bottle. I have left one out for over a week now where I have an abundance of fruit flies. Not a single fly in it, they’re not even interested in these. Save your money and find a working product.

title: Save Your $ & Make A Trap From A Old Water Bottle & Vinegar!
body: A homemade trap from an old water bottle & vinegar with a few drops of soap works better than this any day! This simply doesn't work. The reviewers that say it does must have some bad infestations or something as I've had this in various locations for several weeks and not ONE fruit fly was captured! I even added some foil over the top and poked a few holes as some suggested and it still is a miserable failure!

title: Odd bottle
body: The bottle is odd designed, unprofessional, unpractical.

body: Biggest rip off ever. This item is literally a plastic spice jar of apple cider vinegar, you could make this for 50 cents in less time it would take to order this with items in your kitchen. Actually unreal that i just paid $8 for this, should have read the ingredients. Was specifically trying to not use apple cider vinegar because it stinks. DO NOT BUY! It doesn’t work very well.

title: Didn't work- not a single fly
body: We've been having a massive Fruit Fly issue and been trying everything we could to get it under control. I had high hopes for these but we've had two of them open for a week now and not a single Fruit fly has gone for these. We've moved them around to different areas of our pantry and kitchen and nothing. We've had better luck with homemade traps using dish soap w/ red wine or cider vinegar. They still aren't managing the situation but at least SOME dead flies have resulted from those.

body: I bought a two pack of these….they both collectively caught three gnats. Mind you, I’m having an infestation right now. My own home made ACV and sugar water with dawn dish soap worked way better.

title: Don’t waste your time or money!!
body: This was an absolute freaking waste of money. I am so irritated because it was one of those products that really stood out to me, like no way thousands of people are being dishonest and rating it highly consistently. Boy was I wrong. So, I have a summer time issue with fruit flies (due to fruit). Could not get rid of them for anything. I used the katchy, stem spray, and this product. I had my home PROFESSIONALLY cleaned, opened one of these jars, and left for a 2-week vacation. I just knew I would be coming back to a fruit fly free home thanks to this product working it’s magic. No such luck. I’ll stop there, but just take it from me. It is a waste of money, so don’t get your hopes up.

title: Don’t waist your money!!!
body: If I can give zero stars, I would, but it makes me pick at least one. Total waste of money. I’ve worked in the bar industry for years, I’ve seen barflies congregate around the alcohol for years. I bought this product because it said it was specifically formulated for barflies. At the three days only two barflies were caught in the syrup. I decided to buy another product and filled the bottom cup portion with Jim Bean. Within an hour, there was over a dozen flies caught in the trap. Don’t waste your money. This product does not work.

title: sent an open product
body: we were sent a product that was open, spilled all over the bag and one of the containers was missing half the liquid

title: Disappointed
body: I was having an awful problem with fruit flies in the kitchen and dining room. I read about using apple cider vinegar and water or, even better, Flypunch. I had apple cider vinegar on hand so I tried it first and ordered Flypunch on the same day. After two days of using the apple cider vinegar 95% of the fruit flies were gone. The Flypunch arrived and I figured it would clear up the remaining 5%. That was not the case. After three days of using only the Flypunch, two bottles, the fruit flies were back. I pulled out the apple cider vinegar and the next morning the flies were gone. If you want to get rid of fruit flies first try the apple cider vinegar.

title: Aunt Fannies No Catch Punch
body: This product did not work for me! I have had it out for about a week. There were only two fruit flies captured. I purchased another product which seems to have caught the ones that Aunt Fannies fly punch didn't catch. I absolutely wasted my money.

body: I purchased Aunt Fannie's fly punch fruit fly trap based on all of the encouraging reviews. More wasted money! It smelled just like vinegar when I opened it and left it out for quite a few days with quite a few fruit flies .They were not interested! I have a picture of the open container of the fly punch next to a tuna fish can filled with regular apple cider vinegar and a few pieces of old fruit. Regular apple cider vinegar caught more fruit flies compared to the fly punch which caught none.

title: Boo..
body: Hasn't caught anything!! It ended up getting knocked over... what a mess!! It smells like vinegar. My son found a DIY recipe online and it's only caught a few but it was free!! I did a thorough cleaning with bleach on counters, floors, and cabinets and it's adequate a noticeable difference for today anyway!! Save your money... or throw it away but don't give it to these people!!

title: Well it didn’t work, also leaked out before I got it…
body: When I say this was the biggest disappointment I have come across in along time, I mean it. Now this worked for my friend and was recommended to me so I thought, trusted review from a trusted person so why not. Yeah no, smell is much stronger than regular soap and apple cider vinegar but I was willing to smell( it in a completely different room mind you) as long as it worked. Received the product and both bottles were leaking all over the Amazon package… oh well moving on. Left it out for a couple of days and didn’t catch one bug, not a gnat, not a fruit fly, only attention it caught was mine cause that smell was STRONG. You would have better luck just making a concoction yourself or buying a big light for gnats and fruit flies- that’s what I did when I returned this. Would not recommend to anyone but my enemy.

title: Not worth it for the price
body: I just don’t like it

title: Good concept but not great results
body: Still waiting. One fruit fly caught. My resolution - take caution using - pouring hot water from the tea kettle down all drains - it eradicates living fruit flies and the eggs if they have laid any in your drains. Haven't seen a bug since! To be sure, I have treated every night before bedtime for 4 days. Total success!

title: Sadness and despair
body: One can came empty. Amazon won’t respond I can’t get the seller to respond. So I pours half the liquid from one into the other and set them out. It’s been two days not a single fruit fly. :( I had high hopes but it really doesn’t work for me.

title: Stinks
body: Stinks and leaking. I don’t know why I expected it to have a way too keep the bugs in, like you do when you set up a home made one. But there’s no way to trap them in.

title: Works BUT see the photos attached and you decide
body: The FlyPunch works, BUT,... I had much better luck with a simple household product that didn’t cost me but a few pennies. Both traps were set at the same time 48-52 hours ago. FlyPunch and a bowl of apple cider Venegar with 2-3 drops of dish soap stirred in. Traps were set 3-4 inches apart on the kitchen window. Pictures attached that shows a massive difference between the 2 traps. I was able to count 8 fruit flies in the FlyPunch and far too many to count in the apple cider vinegar mix Can’t say if the FlyPunch would have worked better with the cling wrap, often saw fruit flies sitting on the rim but not too many died. I simply followed the directions on the bottle and did the same with the apple cider trap I googled. 🤷🏽♂️ Left for Thanksgiving and forgot to throw out the bananas, and Shazam,... lots of fruit flies when we returned. 48-52 hours later 99% are gone. You decide which trap worked better.

title: Didn’t work!!
body: Had high hopes this product would work… But… Not one fruit fly took the bate.. very disappointed!

title: Didn't work for me
body: I bought this product because I began to have fruit flies in my apartment. I wanted something easy, something that didn't require much work, so I thought this would be perfect. Just open and forget it. Well after almost two weeks it only caught two fruit flies, just TWO. I was pretty disappointed. I ended up just buying one of those electrical fan things that have a light that are made to trap fruit flies via the fan down onto a glue board. I ran this for two weeks and caught almost 60! So this fan thing worked way better than this liquid. And to top it off, no refunds are allowed. Very shady in my opinion. If my fan trap caught 60 and this liquid caught 2, then it obviously if faulty and I should have the option to get my money back. Do not waste your money on this product.

title: Toxic. Misleading Amazon description.
body: Sorry I ordered this and it will be going down the drain. The description says it’s “plant-based” and “safe around food”. But the label on the product contains several warnings, including to wear rubber gloves when handling and what to do if it gets on your skin. When it’s set up for use it’s an open bottle, just waiting to tip over. It contains Ethyl Lactate: “Ethyl lactate can be harmful if inhaled or absorbed through the skin. Prolonged contact can irritate the skin and eyes, and breathing it in can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, and passing out. Ethyl lactate is flammable and can cause serious or permanent injury”

title: A 100% useless product
body: Completely useless against gnats (fruit flies)...or any other fly infestation. A total BS product. Don't be fooled!

title: 2 stars because it *does* (sort of) work
body: Otherwise 1. Guys. This overpriced apple cider vinegar with a drip of dish soap. The DIY way works way better. Get a clear up, put a few drops of dish soap in it. Pour in apple cider vinegar so that there is a light "soap lining" over the top. Then cover the glass with well stretched cling wrap. Use a fork to poke s few small holes (easy to get on, hard for them to get out which is a big thing this product misses). The fruit flies smell it and crawl into the holes, ho toward the food-smell and get stuck from the layer of soap. They can't crawl out because of the plastic wrap. Bingo. $1 worth of supplies

title: Easy, it just did NOT work
body: Fruit flies were not attracted to it. Easy to use, just remove the lid. The scent is fine, not even detectable, it is a great concept but the t e r r o apple shaped fruit fly traps work 100x better. I actually even used both in my home at the same time and this container was knocked over (This is easy to knock over & waste ALL) and hardly had any caught fruit flies in it when the t e r r o apples had caught as many flies as they could catch, so the one minute it takes to squeeze the liquid into the little apples is definitely worth it even though this natural product just requires a person to remove a lid. title: Trap Doesn't Attract Flies, Spills, Improvement required - Trap Parts Potentially Useful for DIY
body: Trap Doesn't Catch Flies & Spills Unavoidably! Have been using for over a month - haven't caught a single fly (but have other traps that catch smaller flies just fine). This Trap is really no different from small vinegar based fly traps, but is intended to catch larger flies. The flies are supposed to enter the top grid (should be attracted to the weak detergent mixture inside as it smells like weak vinegar which they like), and are supposed to fall into the dilute detergent mixture in the packet sitting inside, which would kill them. But not only did flies seem to be completely not attracted, unfortunately, but the packets are shaped such that you can't attach or remove the grid/lid, without one side of the detergent packet snaps on the legs of the lid, and spills as you open it. So you end up with much less liquid in the trap, which will dry out quickly. I will be trying out my own apple cider vinegar solutions to try to improve the attraction rate, and possibly will add a small amount of detergent, though that may not be required (will require testing), as there seems to be a real gap in the market for a small non-toxic liquid based trap like this, for larger flies (there are plenty of effective vinegar traps for the small flies already). These traps will be worthwhile if I can at lease reuse the casings ... but not sure I can even get that to work yet.

title: Completely Ineffective
body: I bought these traps to put in my kitchen and bathrooms. In our kitchen, we tend to get fruit flies around our coffee machine. In the bathroom, we get them around the sinks, as they come out of the overflow drains and like to hang around my potted plants. These come in a 6-pack, which includes 6 small plastic cases and 6 single-use solution tubs. To setup, you take on plastic case, and one solution tub. Peel the sealed cover off of the solution tub, drop it into the case, and put the lid on the case. From there, you just place it in the area where you notice flying insects. The solution looks unremarkable, visually, but smells slightly of vinegar. After these had dried up, it looked somewhat goopy, but still smelled of vinegar. Putting a bit of water into the solution tub quickly reconstitutes the solution. Given this, I believe the solution is nothing more than vinegar, water, and soap, which is the recipe for a DIY fruit fly trap, but in a MUCH smaller scale. The first night I put these out, I caught a single fruit fly in the bathroom, which made me very hopeful that these were to solution to my problem. Unfortunately, these seem to be absolutely ineffective, as that first fruit fly I caught has been THE ONLY fruit fly I’ve caught, even though you can see them flying around these things. I’m not sure if the solution is too weak, too small amount, or just not an effective solution in the first place. Given that I’ve had these in place for months at this point, and have only caught one single fly, which I believe was a complete fluke, I have to come to the conclusion that these are a complete sham that do absolutely nothing, which the company probably knows, but still decides to cash in on people needing a real solution. Overall, these are a major disappointment, and I would not recommend these to anyone.

The trap contains a liquid that easily spills, so you have to be careful to place it where it isn't at risk of being knocked over (away from kids and kitties, for example). This trap only has a couple more days to perform (the directions say to replace them every two weeks), but I am not too optimistic that I will suddenly see a different outcome from what I've experienced to date. title: Day Spa for Fruit Flies
body: First, the product is not that easy to use. The instructions say to shake well before opening, but it creates a layer of foamy bubbles that take about 15 minutes to dissolve. While the bubbles are present, the fruit flies don't go anywhere close to it. Then the whole product is a jar of some vinegar liquid that is just supposed to be left open on the counter 24 hours a day until all the flies are trapped. It's really easy to tip/spill every where and at 5.4 fl oz, it makes a mess. Second, the scent is awful. It smells like a jar of vinegar (which I could have poured without spending money on this product) and it permeates a 5' radius of where it's located. We kept trying to figure out what was leaking before we realized it was the fruit fly trap. Third, the fruit flies think it's a day spa! They land on the rim and dip down to the top of the liquid, but don't actually fly in the trap. They just chill out around it like we've created a resort for them instead of exterminating. We have other Stem products and love them, but this one was an epic fail!

title: So far not doing anything
body: I got this because I've had small flying bugs occasionally in my home for the last month or 2. Not sure if they're fruit flies, gnats or what else but they are annoying. I figured I'd give this stuff a try (since it's relatively inexpensive. Got it 2 days ago and followed the instructions and got it set up right away. Little bugs are still flying around, so far doesn't look like a single bug has gone into this stuff and it stinks to high heaven. The only thing it's done is change color from the clear look when opened to a honey color (as mention in the directions). Bear in mind I have very few little bugs (usually only "maybe" 1 or 2 in the house but they are still annoying. Since I have this stuff, as long as the stink doesn't drive me totally bonkers I'll leave it and see what happens but I'm not optimistic at this point. I would have expected at least 1 little flying bug to have at least landed on the rim of this container instead of trying to land on my breakfast. Some people say it takes a couple of days to work so I guess we'll see.

title: I was extremely dissappointed in this product
body: I read the directions twice and it is very simple. Shake real good before opening then unscrew the lid off and peel off the protective foil. Then just leave it sitting out on a counter or whatever, near where the fruit flies or gnats seem to be the worse. I would watch the fruit flies crawl all over this product kinda checking it out but it seemed they would always lose interest and go away instead of going for the liquid to get trapped. Now to be fair, I may have caught close to 50 after a couple weeks but when I saw it wasn't working to well, I broke out some fly ribbon paper I had leftover in an old box and the fly ribbon was absolutely covered with them so I won't be wasting any more money on traps like this when I can get 10pc of fly ribbon paper for real cheap. I even have a trick I use. When you hang the flypaper from the ceiling it doesn't really hang down real low and only traps the ones flying up high so I used a regular stick pin and hung a second strip from the one already hanging from the ceiling by sticking the pin into the side of the base, not the bottom, the bottom is too thin to hold it but if you stick it in the side, near the bottom it holds great and now you have two connected that span from the ceiling to about waist level so keep that in mind when doubling them up so as not to place them where you will be bumping into them as they are quite sticky. I really don't like to get less than positive reviews but don't waste your money on this. If you don't like using fly paper then do one of the DIY tricks from youtube with a plastic cup, apple cider, and a bit of saran wrap.

title: needs help!
body: I bought this product to try to get a fruit fly problems under control. In my office at work a co-worker had left a banana out under her desk that we did not know about. We starting getting loads of fruit flies so I decided to give these traps a try. I bought this one and another brand to do some comparison with. The other brand contained only malic acid. I opened them both at the same time and put them out. Immediately fruit flies started collecting around the rim of both containers but none seemed to want to go inside. I waited overnight and this brand had 3 flies in it the next morning and the other brand had only one. Still had dozens sitting around the top edge of the container but none wanted to enter. I looked back at some of the reviews and found one person had used these in combination with a yellow sticky card and said it was very successful. I tried it and believe me it made all the difference in the world. In a short while I had over 20 stuck to the card that I had placed in the jar. Like I said they will work good but just need a little extra help.

They are small, low-profile, and look completely harmless sitting on the counter.Long-Lasting Protection: Each little trap lasts for up to 30 days, and since this comes as a 4-pack, you have more than enough supply to scatter them in multiple problem areas (like near trash cans, houseplants, or recycling bins) or save a couple for the next season.Mess-Free: The liquid stays contained inside the sturdy plastic apple, so you don't have to worry about accidental spills or sticky residue on your countertops.It completely takes the frustration out of dealing with fruit flies. If you want a fast-acting, reliable solution that works exactly as advertised, this TERRO pack is worth every penny. Highly recommended!

title: Mostly effective, and for German roach nymphs
body: These have been somewhat effective. While I have seen less of these pests when I've got this active, I've also seen them literally just hangout on top of the apple. It's like it can see its dead incestuous disgusting family in the goo and it actually takes it as a warning to not proceed. Perhaps I should stop reusing the same trap...Once this stuff runs out, the pests start right back up again. Not as dense as before, but it is noticeable. I'd rather have this than nothing, that's for sure.I wish this came with way more of the liquid. I feel like I have too many apples and not enough liquid. This seller doesn't appear to sell the liquid in bulk, you just have to buy more traps, which is annoying.I also prefer filling it way more than it suggests because if I fill it less, then I have to replace it more frequently. Ergo, providing more of the liquid would be far more useful.This does emit a faint smell, but I've found that it only smells when I'm directly above it.Make sure to tell your guests or family that this thing can spill if you pick it up wrong.I'd ideally rate this maybe 3.5 stars. It works well enough to keep the pests down, but it's not a permanent solution and they don't always fall for the trap.Update: I've changed my mind. Solid 4 stars. I noticed German roach nymphs wading dead in the liquid. I've been keeping these near my sink because that's where the fruit flies hang out. It appears as though the roaches, while trying to get a drink in the sink, find the fruit fly trap and want in. I have a small infestation of roaches in my place, so if they don't fall for one trap, I'm glad they'll fall for another. I don't like having roach traps on my counter due to the chemicals used, so this much-less-poisonous-to-humans trap is a great alternative.

title: So disappointed! No longer recommend. Seller never responded.
body: FRUIT FLY SEASON IS RAPIDLY APPROACHING AND I'M DETERMINED TO PREVENT LAST SUMMER'S INFESTATION. Update : I contacted the company multiple ways and multiple times.Amazon and the company totally ignored my legitimate complaint.  Obviously they don't care about their customers dissatisfaction. It's not about the money - it's about blatant misrepresentation and unethical behavior displayed by both companies. I couldn't even get Amazon to include the "frequently returned" box on the item's page.I bought  three bottles of auntie's product on Amazon 6 days ago to replace my DIY liquid attractant of appl cider vinegar +brown sugar +dish detergent.It's been 5 days and can confirm the other negative reviews that the product CAN'T contain the same liquid attractant - the fruit flies feed on the liquid and are not trapped - they can fly away!!!I unintentionally performed a side by side experiment using this WORTHLESS product against my attractant. Both liquids were placed next to separate hanging cylinders of bright yellow sticky fly paper.I actually watched the flies fly from the  auntie's product into my liquid. Unlike the auntie product, any flies that were not trapped in my DIY liquid were trapped in the fly paper.After 5 days I had to replace the fly paper adjacent to DIY liquid. in contrast, the 3 bottles of Auntie containing who knows what had A TOTAL OF LESS THAN 20 IN THE BOTTLES AND ABOUT 10 TO 20 TRAPPED BY THE FLY PAPER.I am so angry about wasting money on products from Amazon with good reviews. This product has overall rating of 3.8. But that rating is CUMULATIVE - The much older reviews are generally positive compared to more current negative reviews. I conclude this is due to a change in formulation that neither amazon or the seller made clear.I was so pleased that Good Housekeeping had recommended the best way to eliminates fruit fly infestations in a recent article.  The GH panel incorrectly included this product as the only commercially effective liquid attractant since it contained malic acid as part of the formulation. TheFRUIT FLY SEASON article made me remember that I had used Aunties successfully a few summers ago and loved their esthetics and effectiveness.I already emailed a request for them to provide evidence of its effectiveness using a recent bottle.I am requesting a refund from this seller based on my results and will update the status with both responses.Meanwhile if you are battling with fruit flies, infestations made worse by the higher temperature (I live in Connecticut) in the Northeast, read below.First understand that you must use the following steps throughout the fruit fly lifecycle (over several weeks so that the original fruit flies are trapped as well as the their progeny hatched from the hundreds of larvae deposited on whatever they fed on. {I am a biochemist and patent attorney so I needed to know what was going on}.Keep in mind for DIY solutions or other traps that you must attract and rid them from escaping. Otherwise you'll have dead flies near and flying around the attractant.A single fruit fly will deposit hundreds of larvae on fruit and vegetables and existing food sources.Follow these steps :1. Clean all surfaces daily with your typical all purpose cleaner (I use Fantastic with bleach) wherever you find these annoying bugs. For us this is primarily the kitchen in addition to the bathroom and TV room.REMEMBER THEY ARE ATTRACTED TO LIGHT AND 1 FLY WILL DEPOSIT EGGS THAT MATURE IN about 5 to7 DAYS.2. Unfortunately surface cleaning every 1-2 days is necessary to eliminate flying flies you see and larva that will hatch that you can't.3. Immediately thoroughly wash all fruit and vegetables (existing or new) and refrigerate.4. Eliminate All food debris from kitchen counters, microwave, garbage cans, toaster oven,  pet water and food bowls, etc. and keep everything covered or washed like used knives, glassware and plates.5. If you think this is drastic like I did, then you will see an infestation that feels as if those little things won...6. in the article, Good housekeeping recommended this product as using malic acid which is found in apple cider vinegar.  It was part of discussion on using a DIY solution see ingredients above. Any solution must also contain a detergent which causes the flies eating on the attractant  liguid to sink in the solution. They can't fly away and begin a new cycle of depositing eggs. At the beginning of the infestation I used the ingredients above along with standing/hanging yellow sticky fly paper I also bought from Amazon.I am very frustrated that I didn't do the research and work upfront instead of wasting money trying to find the non-existent magic bullet all summer!! As much as I love tasty vine ripened tomatoes and other summer fruit and vegetables, it's just not worth it. I think the high temperatures in July throughout the North East as well as nationaly/globally contributed to the problem experienced by me and almost everyone I know.

title: Works but shouldn't be your only method
body: I had a bad infestation of fruit flies, worse then I have ever experienced this year. Fruit flies can come into your house on produce or they can develop in your drains. The product does work but if you have an infestation of fruit flies you must use several methods to exterminate them which takes time and patience.1. Throw ALL food you keep on your counters. This not only includes fruit but any other food you keep out. Fruit flies are attracted to fermenting foods. I had a mesh bag full of onions in my lazy Susan that I had to throw out because I found the flies in the bag.2. Deep clean your entire kitchen. The fuit flies continue the reproduce because they are laying their eggs on surfaces that are dirty. They can lay up to 500 eggs a day so if the adults keep having places to land aka fruit and sticky surfaces they will continue to reproduce. This means taking out everything on your counter and spraying with a cleaner solution.3. Last but not least, you need to find the source! Fruit flies can breed in your kitchen drain. This means using a solution to pour down the drain to kill the flies and eggs. There is solutions sold on Amazon that can be used. This needs several treatments and ensure your sink is always clean.In conclusion, you can get ride of fruit flies but it takes time. For me it took about 2 weeks. If you only use this trap, its just catching the flies but they will still reproduce if you don't give them a place to breed. Along with these traps, I made my own with apple cider vinegar. I deep cleaned my kitchen and bought the solution used to treat the sink for flies. One you kill the breeding ground, you just continue to set traps until the last adults are gone.Good Luck!

title: Only thing that worked!!
body: For some reason, this summer was bad for fruit flies at our home. We also had an invasion of these strange flies that looked like mini house flies whose wings folded completely over their bodies... no idea what they were.Anyhoo, the long and short of it is that I watched a $÷!+ ton of TikTok videos and tried what seemed like a gazillion "fruitless" methods of ridding my home of the Amityville Horror invasion of flies. None of them worked.  I purchased fly strips that were allegedly scented to attract flies, apparently they dont smell appealing to these flies. I purchased sticky fly boards, I think I caught approximately 12 fruit flies as I frustratedly swung the board through the cloud of flies on my way to deposit it in the trash we had moved outside in a bid to mitigate the buggers.I remembered seeing this advertised late last winter when I purchased some Aunt Fannie's carpet fresh and I searched Amazon until I found it. My mom lives next door and she was under attack as well so I purchased a 2 pack!Fast forward to the arrival and within an hour of me putting this fly ninja stuff out I had trapped and drowned more flies than I had in the entire month of TikTok tries and strips/boards combined!It's a jar of vinegar and perhaps soap? I put it on the window sill above my sink and they dip in for a looky loo and never come out!Well worth the price to find that apple cider vinegar really does lure those flying germ spreaders in!Hands down the best at riding my house of both types of flies and I will purchase again! They worked equally well for my mom and she says she is purchasing the next 2 pack we need ;)

title: Amazingly effective!
body: We've been having a serious fruit fly/gnat infestation for years, and I'm almost positive they're breeding somewhere in our walls, floors or ceilings -- we've had leaks in the past, and I think we still do. So while it may take more than a trap to eradicate the gnat population here, this trap has brought us substantial relief, in just the span of 2-3 days.We can't call in the professionals at this point, for reasons I can't go into, but since the weather got warmer this spring, life in our small apartment was becoming unbearable. They were flying into our faces, landing on us, and landing in or on our food, even as we prepared it or ate it.I don't think it's been more than 48 hours, and there are A LOT of dead flies in the trap.We've caught substantial numbers with both homemade vinegar traps and the electronic Katchees, but this trap seems to summon the gnats, even from other rooms of the apartment (the trap is in the bedroom, but we also have a combination kitchen/LR, a bathroom and a foyer).Be warned, the trap does have a strict vinegar smell that wafts around, but the smell is NOTHING in comparison to the nuisance of the gnats.They do hang around the rim of the trap for a while, but then they definitely fly into it and die. We put it in an awkward place, and I don't want to take the chance of spilling it, so I can't get anything close to a count, but not only can I glimpse a large quantity of dead gnats, but I haven't seen ANY flying or landing anywhere else in our place, in many hours. This is truly amazing.I don't expect that it will eradicate them completely, because we don't know the breeding source, but one can always hope that all breeding adults will eventually fly around and find this thing. Until then, we may have to keep replacing the traps and finding ways to stretch out the liquid. Maybe we'll post an update, at some point.Meanwhile, I THANK GOD for the blessing of having this trap to control the terrible nuisance that was making our lives so unpleasant and difficult.Posting this update about 2-3 weeks later -- unfortunately in the warm weather (and we don't have air conditioning), these gnats are multiplying faster than the trap can catch them. Without it, we'd probably be swamped in gnats, fruit flies and whatever all these pests are. We'll have to put more traps around.

title: Day Spa for Fruit Flies
body: First, the product is not that easy to use. The instructions say to shake well before opening, but it creates a layer of foamy bubbles that take about 15 minutes to dissolve. It's really easy to tip/spill every where and at 5.4 fl oz, it makes a mess.Second, the scent is awful. It smells like a jar of vinegar (which I could have poured without spending money on this product) and it permeates a 5' radius of where it's located. We kept trying to figure out what was leaking before we realized it was the fruit fly trap.Third, the fruit flies think it's a day spa! They land on the rim and dip down to the top of the liquid, but don't actually fly in the trap. They just chill out around it like we've created a resort for them instead of exterminating.We have other Stem products and love them, but this one was an epic fail!

title: I was extremely dissappointed in this product
body: I read the directions twice and it is very simple. Shake real good before opening then unscrew the lid off and peel off the protective foil. Then just leave it sitting out on a counter or whatever, near where the fruit flies or gnats seem to be the worse. I would watch the fruit flies crawl all over this product kinda checking it out but it seemed they would always lose interest and go away instead of going for the liquid to get trapped. Now to be fair, I may have caught close to 50 after a couple weeks but when I saw it wasn't working to well, I broke out some fly ribbon paper I had leftover in an old box and the fly ribbon was absolutely covered with them so I won't be wasting any more money on traps like this when I can get 10pc of fly ribbon paper for real cheap. I even have a trick I use. When you hang the flypaper from the ceiling it doesn't really hang down real low and only traps the ones flying up high so I used a regular stick pin and hung a second strip from the one already hanging from the ceiling by sticking the pin into the side of the base, not the bottom, the bottom is too thin to hold it but if you stick it in the side, near the bottom it holds great and now you have two connected that span from the ceiling to about waist level so keep that in mind when doubling them up so as not to place them where you will be bumping into them as they are quite sticky. I really don't like to get less than positive reviews but don't waste your money on this. If you don't like using fly paper then do one of the DIY tricks from youtube with a plastic cup, apple cider, and a bit of saran wrap.

title: Super Ninja Fruit Fly Traps: bait useless for my fruit flies while Terro brand bait has worked well.
body: I tried 3 different brands of liquid fruit fly attractant: in this home for 25 yrs but had never had a fruit fly problem in my life, they must have come in w/fruit which we don't buy a lot of: found out one female lays 500 eggs...This product, Super Ninja Fruit fly traps- I put several of these pre-filled bottles out for days but SUPER NINJA FRUIT FLY TRAPS DID NOT CATCH A SINGLE FRUIT FLY, compared to Terro brand used in the red plastic tomatoes, which worked well. I even tried the Super Ninja bait in the red Terro plastic tomatoe containers as some ads claimed the color + shape of the vessel played a role in attracting bugs but still no luck. The excellent Terro brand even worked well in a clear glass baby food jar.Terro works well, I see several of the fruit flies in the liquid. However, the tomatoe shaped plastic holders can tip easy, its a sticky, stinky liquid for which the company in South America would not tell me if it has a percent of poison in it- many of their products do, + they only give the number of poison control, + insist that the formula is 'proprietary information'. But after trying 3 brands, will stick w/Terro even though it does not sell a large container of liquid (I do not need more plastic tomatoe holders  plus glass baby food jars worked just as well)Have put the Terro liquid bait-filled plastic tomatoes in clear plastic cups (clear so insects could see the red fruit shape), as the tomatoes have many preferations, which is good, but they are light-weight, tip + spill easily.However, the flat rectangular shape of the bottles of the Super Ninja Fruit fly Traps, though the liquid they came with is useless, the bottles w/their flat walls can be attached to any flat surface or wall w/a sticky strip; That had been my intent when I ordered them so I did not have to worry about containers spilling or space to put them down in or my cat getting to one... As the Ninja contents have proved useless, I will empty + rinse them out so I can fill them w/Terro attractant. will report if the insects will use these glass containers.While I had planned to take advantage of the flat walls of the Ninja glass containers + a photo in the Ad may have suggested they could be stuck to a wall, I was surprised that they came w/a pre-attached silicone sticky strip pre-attached for that purpose (one should use a spatula to remove the sticky strip and bottle intact from the wall (they are silicone w/adhesive + residue can be easily removed).There was one other brand of 25 vials which also did not catch a single fruit fly- even when used in Terro's tomatoe shape, which I also do not recommend, 'Qualirey 20 Pack Fruit Fly Trap Refill Liquid'...Do not recommend the Super Ninja Fly Traps because the bait does not work, at least for my fruit flies in Connecticut; but I still need to substitute Terro liquid bait in their their rectangular glass containers a+ see if the insects will then use them before I formally recommend the containers themselves- they have a yellow funnel on top. However, $39.99 plus tax is a high price to pay for the 12 glass containers which I will need to empty out to use with Terro brand liquid- if the bugs will use that container w/Terro bait.

title: Completely Ineffective
body: I bought these traps to put in my kitchen and bathrooms.  In our kitchen, we tend to get fruit flies around our coffee machine.  In the bathroom, we get them around the sinks, as they come out of the overflow drains and like to hang around my potted plants.These come in a 6-pack, which includes 6 small plastic cases and 6 single-use solution tubs.To setup, you take on plastic case, and one solution tub.  Peel the sealed cover off of the solution tub, drop it into the case, and put the lid on the case.  From there, you just place it in the area where you notice flying insects.The solution looks unremarkable, visually, but smells slightly of vinegar.  After these had dried up, it looked somewhat goopy, but still smelled of vinegar.  Putting a bit of water into the solution tub quickly reconstitutes the solution.  Given this, I believe the solution is nothing more than vinegar, water, and soap, which is the recipe for a DIY fruit fly trap, but in a MUCH smaller scale.The first night I put these out, I caught a single fruit fly in the bathroom, which made me very hopeful that these were to solution to my problem.  Unfortunately, these seem to be absolutely ineffective, as that first fruit fly I caught has been THE ONLY fruit fly I’ve caught, even though you can see them flying around these things.  I’m not sure if the solution is too weak, too small amount, or just not an effective solution in the first place.Given that I’ve had these in place for months at this point, and have only caught one single fly, which I believe was a complete fluke, I have to come to the conclusion that these are a complete sham that do absolutely nothing, which the company probably knows, but still decides to cash in on people needing a real solution.Overall, these are a major disappointment, and I would not recommend these to anyone.

title: Trap Doesn't Attract Flies, Spills, Improvement required - Trap Parts Potentially Useful for DIY
body: Trap Doesn't Catch Flies & Spills Unavoidably! Have been using for over a month - haven't caught a single fly (but have other traps that catch smaller flies just fine). This Trap is really no different from small vinegar based fly traps, but is intended to catch larger flies. The flies are supposed to enter the top grid (should be attracted to the weak detergent mixture inside as it smells like weak vinegar which they like), and are supposed to fall into the dilute detergent mixture in the packet sitting inside, which would kill them. But not only did flies seem to be completely not attracted, unfortunately, but the packets are shaped such that you can't attach or remove the grid/lid, without one side of the detergent packet snaps on the legs of the lid, and spills as you open it. So you end up with much less liquid in the trap, which will dry out quickly.I will be trying out my own apple cider vinegar solutions to try to improve the attraction rate, and possibly will add a small amount of detergent, though that may not be required (will require testing), as there seems to be a real gap in the market for a small non-toxic liquid based trap like this, for larger flies (there are plenty of effective vinegar traps for the small flies already). These traps will be worthwhile if I can at lease reuse the casings ... but not sure I can even get that to work yet.

---

I am currently living in an active infestation. I have no idea where
these creatures came from or how they managed to establish a thriving
civilization so quickly, having deep-cleaned my room and offering
absolutely no food, water, or emotional support to these bugs. And yet,
they have moved in and declared sovereignty.

launch themselves into your face like kamikaze pilots.

around it like it's a sketchy bar.

DOES NOT WORK. I have a gnat infestation in my indoor office plants.
Because they are in my office, where I spend 8 hours per day, I needed
them gone, stat. I tried 3 different methods of gnat elimination: (1)
Terro apple-shaped fly traps; (2) Shallow dishes of liquid dish soap;
(3) Zevo plug-in flying insect trap.

After 3 days, here are the results:

\(1\) Terro apple-shaped fly traps: Easy to set up and fill with their
"special" gnat-attracting formula which I am sure is just apple cider
vinegar. The apple containers are small and cute. But, they don't work.
I CAUGHT 1 (ONE) GNAT using 4 different traps placed on top of soil in
my plant containers.

\(2\) Shallow dishes of dawn dish soap: Easy to set up and fill.
However, the liquid soap starts to dry out and harden after several
days. They are a bit of a pain to wash out and refill, icks me out, plus
I think it's a waste of dish soap. I CAUGHT 50 GNATS using this
method--I used 4 different shallow containers placed on top of soil in
my plant containers.

\(3\) Zevo plug-in flying insect trap. This plug-in fly trap was super
easy to set up. It's basically a blue light that attracts the insects
and super sticky paper (comes with replacement inserts) to trap them. I
CAUGHT 40 GNATS using this method. This trap is the furthest from my
plants--it's about 6 feet away. If I move it closer, it will probably
work even better. This is my favorite scent-free, mess-free method that
actually works.

If I didn't use the other 2 methods, I would have about 100 more gnats
still flying around my office space, ick. Save your money and don't
buy.

I made a couple of do-it-yourself traps. There are a couple of them on
the internet. It's apple cider vinegar in a mason jar with small holes

mysteries.

a few.

The most effective (and most fun) is to use our Dyson stick vacuum. We
have white cabinets, so it's easy to see the files when they land.
I've observed that they tend to like vertical surfaces and generally
orient themselves head-up. They also take off backwards. So, if you get
the vacuum running on high and sneak up on them from below, you can
generally suck them in. At least for me, this has some entertainment
value. My wife tells me that I remind her of Bill Murray in Ghostbusters
with that thing. But it definitely does work. Who you gonna call\...?

Bottom line\... I haven't found any magic solution to the problem.
Everything seems to work about equally well. I have my homemade traps,
the Terro traps and the light trap all deployed. There is some value in
purchasing the Terro traps, because they are the most attractive option.

up on their "attractant". Apple cider vinegar and dishwasher detergent
should be an effective substitute.

This Hot Shot pack contains 6 low profile traps designed to attract and
"eliminate" flying insects. For use in the kitchen, I WAY prefer these
over the hanging sticky fly traps! These take up little space, conceal
dead flys and are visually neutral. Once opened, these traps have a
maximum effectiveness of 2 weeks. The only downside to these is the
liquid bait. Inside the case is a little plastic tub with a sealed foil
top. You remove the foil, exposing the liquid bait. Put the tub back
into the case and replace the lid, then set the trap wherever you want
it. Provided you are careful, you shouldn't have an issue with spilling
the bait, but this is not an item that should be shifted around
frequently. And you certainly won't want it to be within reach of young
children. Otherwise, this is a fine product for eliminating flys
wherever they gather.

I ordered the set of six Hot Shot Flying Insect Traps based on my
experience with the aerosol version of the Hot Shot Flying Insect
Killer. The aerosol version works very well. I set out three traps in my
kitchen to capture a group of fruit flies that were able to be fruitful
and multiply while my family and I were away from our home for a few
days. As the day progressed there were fewer and fewer fruit flies until
there were none. I held back three of the plastic traps to take care of
any fruit flies that may hatch from eggs; however, I suspect that I will
not need to set them out since the initial three traps have a14-day
effectiveness window.

The Hot Shot traps are small and discreet and do not secrete any
discernible smell until you remove the plastic top and tear off the foil
seal. Be careful when removing the foil seal -- the bait is liquid.
There is a slight smell from the bait, but it is barely discernible
unless you hold your nose to the trap. I like how once the traps have
done their job one can easily dispose of them in the trash.

This is a useful product. The Hot Shot traps are simple, easy to use,
and thorough in their ability to decrease and eventually eliminate my
unwelcome colony of fruit files. I cannot wait until spring and summer
to deploy them and see them take out the house files.
